title.raw: 卷65 邢巒 李平 Volume 65: Xing Luan, Li Ping

sentences.zh: 邢巒 李平

translations.literal: Xing Luan, Li Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan and Li Ping.

sentences.zh: 邢巒，字洪賓，河間鄚人也。

translations.literal: Xing Luan, styled Hongbin, was a native of Mo in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan, courtesy name Hongbin, came from Mo in Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: [1]五世祖嘏，石勒頻徵，不至。

translations.literal: [1] His fifth-generation ancestor Gu was repeatedly summoned by Shi Le but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: [1] His fifth-generation ancestor Gu was summoned repeatedly by Shi Le but never answered the call.

sentences.zh: 嘏無子，巒高祖蓋，自旁宗入後。

translations.literal: Gu had no son; Luan's great-grandfather Gai entered the line as heir from a collateral branch.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had no son, so Luan's great-grandfather Gai was adopted into the line from a collateral branch of the clan.

sentences.zh: 蓋孫穎，字宗敬，以才學知名。

translations.literal: Gai's grandson Ying, styled Zongjing, was renowned for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's grandson Ying, courtesy name Zongjing, won fame for his learning and ability.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，與范陽盧玄、勃海高允等同時被徵。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizu, he was summoned at the same time as Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he was summoned to court together with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, and others.

sentences.zh: 後拜中書侍郎，假通直常侍、寧朔將軍、平城子，銜命使於劉義隆。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, acting as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the North, and Marquis of Pingcheng, and was sent on mission to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Vice Director of the Secretariat and, with acting rank as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the North, and Marquis of Pingcheng, carried an imperial commission to Liu Yilong's court.

sentences.zh: 後以病還鄉里。

translations.literal: Later, because of illness, he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，世祖訪穎於羣臣曰：「往憶邢穎長者，有學義，宜侍講東宮，今其人安在？

translations.literal: After a long while, Emperor Shizu inquired among the ministers about Ying, saying: "I recall in the past the elder Xing Ying, learned and principled, fit to lecture in the Eastern Palace—where is that man now?
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Emperor Taiwu asked his ministers about Ying: "I still remember the elder Xing Ying—a man of learning and integrity who ought to lecture in the Eastern Palace. Where is he now?

sentences.zh: 」司徒崔浩對曰：「穎臥疾在家。

translations.literal: " The Minister of Education Cui Hao replied: "Ying lies ill at home.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Education Cui Hao answered, "Ying is bedridden at home.

sentences.zh: 」世祖遣太醫馳驛就療。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent the imperial physician post-haste by relay to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor dispatched the court physician by urgent relay to treat him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、定州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously given the title General Who Establishes Valor and Governor of Dingzhou, with the posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as General Who Establishes Valor and Governor of Dingzhou, with the posthumous epithet Kang.

sentences.zh: 子脩年，即巒父也，州主簿。

translations.literal: His son Xiunian, who was Luan's father, served as chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiunian—Luan's father—served as chief clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 巒少而好學，負帙尋師，家貧厲節，遂博覽書傳。

translations.literal: Luan from youth loved learning, shouldered his satchel to seek teachers, and though his family was poor upheld his integrity, until he broadly read books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Luan loved study; he carried his books from teacher to teacher, and though his household was poor he held fast to his principles until he had read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 有文才幹略，美鬚髯，姿貌甚偉。

translations.literal: He had literary talent and strategic ability, a handsome beard, and a very imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed literary talent and strategic sense, a fine beard, and a strikingly imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 州郡表貢，拜中書博士，遷員外散騎侍郎，為高祖所知賞。

translations.literal: The province and commandery recommended him for tribute; he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat, promoted to Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and came to be known and favored by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by his province and commandery, he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat, then promoted to Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and won the notice and esteem of Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 兼員外散騎常侍，使於蕭賾，還，拜通直郎，轉中書侍郎，甚見顧遇，常參座席。

translations.literal: He also served as Supernumerary Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and was sent on mission to Xiao Ze; on his return he was appointed Attendant of Direct Communication, then transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, was greatly favored, and regularly took part in the emperor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Supernumerary Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary on a mission to Xiao Ze of Southern Qi. On his return he was made Attendant of Direct Communication and then Vice Director of the Secretariat, enjoyed exceptional favor, and was often present at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 高祖因行藥至司空府南，見巒宅，遣使謂巒曰：「朝行藥至此，見卿宅乃住，東望德館，情有依然。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, while taking his constitutional walk, came south of the Minister of Works' residence, saw Luan's house, and sent a messenger to say to Luan: "On my morning walk I came here, saw your house, and stopped; looking east toward your hall of virtue, my feelings are as of old.
translations.idiomatic: While taking his morning constitutional, Emperor Xiaowen came to the south of the Minister of Works' residence, saw Luan's home, and sent a messenger to say: "On my walk this morning I came this far, saw your house, and stopped. Gazing east toward your hall, the old feeling returns.

sentences.zh: 」巒對曰：「陛下移構中京，方建無窮之業，臣意在與魏昇降，寧容不務永年之宅。

translations.literal: " Luan replied: "Your Majesty has moved the capital to the central metropolis and is just now building an enterprise without end; this subject's intent is to rise and fall with Wei—how could he fail to strive for a dwelling of lasting years?"
translations.idiomatic: " Luan replied, "Your Majesty has moved the capital to the central metropolis and is building an enterprise without end. My wish is to rise and fall with Wei—how could I trouble myself with a house meant to last forever?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖謂司空穆亮、僕射李沖曰：「巒之此言，其意不小。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu said to the Minister of Works Mu Liang and the Vice Director Li Chong: "In this remark of Luan's, his intent is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowen said to Minister of Works Mu Liang and Vice Director Li Chong, "In those words Luan's ambition is no small thing.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏策秀、孝，詔曰：「秀、孝殊問，經權異策，邢巒才清，可令策秀。」

translations.literal: " The responsible offices memorialized on examining the Cultivated and the Filial; an edict said: "The Cultivated and the Filial have different questions, the constant and the expedient have different examinations; Xing Luan's talent is pure—let him be examined for the Cultivated."
translations.idiomatic: " When the responsible offices reported on the examinations for the Cultivated Talent and Filial Piety categories, an edict read: "The Cultivated and the Filial call for different questions and different standards of judgment. Xing Luan's talent is outstanding—assign him the Cultivated examination."

sentences.zh: 後兼黃門郎。

translations.literal: Later he also served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He later also served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 從征漢北，巒在新野，後至。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign north of the Han; Luan was at Xinye and arrived late.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the campaign north of the Han. Luan was at Xinye and arrived late.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「伯玉天迷其心，鬼惑其慮，守危邦，固逆主，乃至如此。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Boyu is heaven-bewitched in heart and demon-deluded in counsel, holding a doomed state and stubbornly opposing his lord, until it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "Boyu's heart is lost to heaven and his counsel deluded by demons. He holds a doomed state yet clings to a rebellious master, and things have come to this pass.

sentences.zh: 」巒曰：「新野既摧，眾城悉潰，唯有伯玉，不識危機，平殄之辰，事在旦夕。

translations.literal: " Luan said: "Xinye is already crushed and the host of cities have all collapsed; only Boyu does not recognize the crisis—the day of complete annihilation is a matter of morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: " Luan said, "Xinye is already destroyed and the other cities have all fallen. Only Boyu fails to see the danger. The hour of his complete destruction is only a matter of days.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「至此以來，雖未擒滅，城隍已崩，想在不遠。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu said: "From this point on, though he has not yet been captured and destroyed, his walls and moats have already collapsed; I think it is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowen said, "From this point on, though he has not yet been taken, his defenses are already broken. I think the end is near.

sentences.zh: 所以緩攻者，正待中書為露布耳。

translations.literal: The reason for slowing the attack is precisely to wait for the Secretariat to write the victory bulletin.
translations.idiomatic: The reason we are holding back the assault is simply to wait for the Secretariat to draft the victory proclamation."

sentences.zh: 」尋除正黃門、兼御史中尉、瀛州大中正，遷散騎常侍、兼尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Regular Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Imperial Censor-in-Chief and Senior Rectifier of Yingzhou, then promoted to Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Regular Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Imperial Censor-in-Chief and Senior Rectifier of Yingzhou, then promoted to Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，巒奏曰：「臣聞昔者明王之以德治天下，莫不重粟帛，輕金寶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, Luan memorialized: "Your subject has heard that in antiquity enlightened kings who governed the realm by virtue all valued grain and silk and made light of gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign Luan memorialized: "I have heard that the enlightened kings of old who ruled the realm through virtue all prized grain and silk and held gold and jewels lightly.

sentences.zh: 然粟帛安國育民之方，金玉是虛華損德之物。

translations.literal: For grain and silk are the means to settle the state and nurture the people, while gold and jade are empty show that injure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and silk are what settle the state and nourish the people; gold and jade are mere vanity that erode moral character.

sentences.zh: 故先皇深觀古今，去諸奢侈。

translations.literal: Therefore the late emperor deeply surveyed past and present and removed all extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the late emperor looked deeply into past and present and cast off every extravagance.

sentences.zh: 服御尚質，不貴雕鏤，所珍在素，不務奇綺，至乃以紙絹為帳扆，銅鐵為轡勒。

translations.literal: For dress and equipage he prized simplicity, did not value carving and inlay, treasured plainness and did not pursue strange brocades, even to the point of using paper and silk for screens and curtains and copper and iron for bridle and bit.
translations.idiomatic: He valued simplicity in dress and equipage, scorned carving and inlay, prized the plain over the ornate, and even used paper and silk for screens and copper and iron for bridle fittings.

sentences.zh: 訓朝廷以節儉，示百姓以憂務，日夜孜孜，小大必慎。

translations.literal: He instructed the court in frugality, showed the people his anxious diligence, and day and night worked tirelessly, careful in matters great and small.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the court frugality, showed the people his anxious concern for public affairs, and toiled day and night, careful in matters large and small.

sentences.zh: 輕賤珠璣，示其無設，府藏之金，裁給而已，更不買積以費國資。

translations.literal: He made light of pearls and gems to show that he had no use for them; the gold in the treasury was only enough to supply needs, and he no longer bought and hoarded it to waste state resources.
translations.idiomatic: He held pearls and gems cheap to show he had no need of them. The gold in the treasury was only enough to meet immediate needs; he no longer bought and stockpiled it at the state's expense.

sentences.zh: 逮景明之初，承升平之業，四疆清晏，遠邇來同，於是蕃貢繼路，商賈交入，諸所獻貿，倍多於常。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the Jingming era, inheriting an age of rising peace, the four borders were clear and calm and near and far alike came in harmony; then tribute from the frontier followed one road after another, merchants and traders entered in succession, and all goods presented were more than twice the usual.
translations.idiomatic: By the opening of the Jingming era, inheriting an age of peace, the four borders were tranquil and subjects near and far were at one. Tribute missions lined the roads, merchants came and went, and the goods presented were more than twice the usual amount.

sentences.zh: 雖加以節約，猶歲損萬計，珍貨常有餘，國用恒不足。

translations.literal: Even with added economy, there was still an annual loss counted in the tens of thousands; precious goods were constantly in surplus while state expenditures were always insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Even with added restraint, the annual loss still ran to tens of thousands. Precious goods piled up while state funds were always short.

sentences.zh: 若不裁其分限，便恐無以支歲。

translations.literal: If their allotments are not cut back, I fear there will be no way to support the year.
translations.idiomatic: Unless their allotments are cut back, I fear the treasury will not last the year.

sentences.zh: 自今非為要須者，請皆不受。

translations.literal: From now on, what is not truly necessary, I ask that all of it be refused.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, I ask that everything not truly necessary be refused."

sentences.zh: 」世宗從之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 尋正尚書，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made full Director of the Secretariat, his regular attendant post remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made full Director of the Secretariat while retaining his post as Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍梁秦二州行事夏侯道遷以漢中內附，詔加巒使持節、都督征梁漢諸軍事、假鎮西將軍，進退徵攝，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's acting commissioner of Liang and Qin provinces, Xiahou Daoyian, brought Hanzhong over to allegiance within the borders; an edict added for Luan the credential of envoy bearing the staff, command over all armies campaigning against Liang and Han, and acting rank as General Who Pacifies the West, with authority to advance and withdraw, levy and take, and act as expedient required.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan's acting commissioner of Liang and Qin, Xiahou Daoyian, surrendered Hanzhong to Wei, an edict appointed Luan envoy bearing the staff, commander of all armies campaigning against Liang and Han, and acting General Who Pacifies the West, with full authority to advance, withdraw, levy troops, and act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 巒至漢中，白馬已西猶未歸順，巒遣寧遠將軍楊舉、統軍楊眾愛、汜洪雅等領卒六千討之。

translations.literal: When Luan reached Hanzhong, west of Baima there were still places that had not submitted; Luan sent the General Who Establishes Distance, Yang Ju, the army commander Yang Zhong'ai, Si Hongya, and others leading six thousand soldiers to subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan reached Hanzhong, the region west of Baima had not yet submitted. He sent General Who Establishes Distance Yang Ju, army commander Yang Zhong'ai, Si Hongya, and others at the head of six thousand men to subdue it.

sentences.zh: 軍鋒所臨，賊皆款附，唯補谷戍主何法靜據城拒守。

translations.literal: Wherever the army's van arrived, the enemy all sincerely submitted; only the garrison commander of Bugu, He Fajing, held the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the army's van went, the enemy submitted—only He Fajing, commander of the Bugu garrison, held his city and resisted.

sentences.zh: 舉等進師討之，[2]法靜奔潰，乘勝追奔至關城之下，蕭衍龍驤將軍關城流雜

translations.literal: Ju and the others advanced to attack. [2] Fajing fled in rout; pressing the victory in pursuit, they chased to below Guancheng, where Xiao Yan's Dragon-Cavalry General Guancheng liu za
translations.idiomatic: Ju and the others advanced to attack. [2] Fajing broke and fled. Pursuing in victory, they chased as far as Guancheng, where Xiao Yan's Dragon-Cavalry General Guancheng liu za

translations.literal: 〈Doubtful〉
translations.idiomatic: Passage marked doubtful.

sentences.zh: 李侍叔逆以城降。

translations.literal: Li Shishu thereupon surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shishu thereupon surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍輔國將軍任僧幼等三十餘將，率南安、廣長、東洛、大寒、武始、除口、平溪、桶谷諸郡之民七千餘戶，相繼而至。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Ren Sengyou and more than thirty other generals led over seven thousand households of the people of Nan'an, Guangchang, Dongluo, Dahan, Wushi, Chukou, Pingxi, Tonggu, and other commanderies, arriving one after another.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty of Xiao Yan's generals, including General Who Assists the State Ren Sengyou, led over seven thousand households from Nan'an, Guangchang, Dongluo, Dahan, Wushi, Chukou, Pingxi, Tonggu, and other commanderies to surrender in succession.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍平西將軍李天賜、晉壽太守王景胤等擁眾七千，屯據石亭。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's General Who Pacifies the West Li Tianci, the Administrator of Jinshou Wang Jingyin, and others mustered a host of seven thousand and encamped at Shiting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's General Who Pacifies the West Li Tianci, Administrator of Jinshou Wang Jingyin, and others gathered seven thousand men and encamped at Shiting.

sentences.zh: 統軍韓多寶等率眾擊之，破天賜前軍趙䐗，擒斬一千三百。

translations.literal: The army commander Han Duobao and others led troops to attack them, defeated Tianci's vanguard Zhao Zhe, and captured and beheaded thirteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Han Duobao and others attacked them, routed Tianci's vanguard Zhao Zhe, and killed or captured thirteen hundred men.

sentences.zh: 遣統軍李義珍討晉壽，景胤宵遁，遂平之。

translations.literal: He sent the army commander Li Yizhen to attack Jinshou; Jingyin fled by night, and it was thereupon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He sent army commander Li Yizhen against Jinshou. Jingyin fled by night and the place was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「巒至彼，須有板官，以懷初附，高下品第，可依征義陽都督之格也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When Luan reaches there, there must be provisional officials to win over those newly submitting; grades high and low may follow the standard used for the commander who campaigned against Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "When Luan arrives there he must appoint provisional officials to win over the newly submitted population. Ranks high and low may follow the standard used in the Yiyang campaign."

sentences.zh: 」拜巒使持節、安西將軍、梁秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: " Luan was appointed envoy bearing the staff, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of the two provinces of Liang and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was appointed envoy bearing the staff, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Liang and Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍巴西太守龐景民恃遠不降，巒遣巴州刺史嚴玄思往攻之，斬景民，巴西悉平。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Administrator of Baxi Pang Jingmin, relying on distance, would not submit; Luan sent the Governor of Bazhou Yan Xuansi to attack him, beheaded Jingmin, and Baxi was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's Administrator of Baxi, Pang Jingmin, trusting in his distance from the capital, refused to submit. Luan sent Governor of Bazhou Yan Xuansi against him, executed Jingmin, and pacified all of Baxi.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其冠軍將軍孔陵等率眾二萬，屯據深坑，冠軍將軍魯方達固南安，[3]冠軍將軍任僧褒、輔國將軍李畎戍石同。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his General Who Establishes the Host Kong Ling and others leading a host of twenty thousand to encamp at Shenkeng; the General Who Establishes the Host Lu Fangda held Nan'an firm, [3] the General Who Establishes the Host Ren Sengbao and the General Who Assists the State Li Quan garrisoned Shitong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent his General Who Establishes the Host Kong Ling and others with twenty thousand men to hold Shenkeng. General Who Establishes the Host Lu Fangda fortified Nan'an, [3] while General Who Establishes the Host Ren Sengbao and General Who Assists the State Li Quan garrisoned Shitong.

sentences.zh: 巒統軍王足所在擊破之，梟衍輔國將軍樂保明、寧朔將軍李伯度、龍驤將軍李思賢，賊遂保回車柵。

translations.literal: Luan's army commander Wang Zu, wherever he went, defeated them, took the heads of Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Yue Baoming, General Who Pacifies the North Li Baidu, and Dragon-Cavalry General Li Sixian, and the enemy then held the Huiche stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Luan's commander Wang Zu fought he broke the enemy, beheaded Xiao Yan's Generals Who Assists the State Yue Baoming, Who Pacifies the North Li Baidu, and Dragon-Cavalry Li Sixian, and the enemy fell back to the Huiche stockade.

sentences.zh: 足又進擊衍輔國將軍范峻，自餘斬獲殆將萬數。

translations.literal: Zu again advanced to attack Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fan Jun; besides these, those beheaded and captured nearly reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zu advanced again against Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fan Jun. All told, the killed and captured nearly reached ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 孔陵等收集遺眾，奔保梓潼，足又破之，斬衍輔國將軍符伯度，其殺傷投溺者萬有餘人。

translations.literal: Kong Ling and the others gathered the remnant host and fled to hold Zitong; Zu again defeated them and beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fu Baidu; those killed, wounded, and drowned exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ling gathered the survivors and fled to Zitong. Zu defeated them again and beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fu Baidu. Those killed, wounded, or drowned exceeded ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 開地定民，東西七百，南北千里，獲郡十四、二部護軍及諸縣戍，遂逼涪城。

translations.literal: They opened territory and settled the people—seven hundred li east to west and a thousand li north to south—taking fourteen commanderies, two Protector-General departments, and garrisons of various counties, and thus pressed on Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: They opened territory and settled the people across seven hundred li east to west and a thousand li north to south, took fourteen commanderies, two Protector-General districts, and numerous county garrisons, and pressed on to Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 巒表曰：

translations.literal: Luan memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized:

sentences.zh: 揚州、成都相去萬里，陸途既絕，唯資水路。

translations.literal: Yangzhou and Chengdu are ten thousand li apart; the land route is already cut, and they rely solely on the water route.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou and Chengdu lie ten thousand li apart. The land route is cut off; they depend entirely on the waterways.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍兄子淵藻，去年四月十三日發揚州，今歲四月四日至蜀。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's elder brother's son Yuanzao set out from Yangzhou on the thirteenth day of the fourth month last year and reached Shu on the fourth day of the fourth month this year.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's nephew Yuanzao left Yangzhou on the thirteenth day of the fourth month last year and reached Shu on the fourth day of the fourth month this year.

sentences.zh: 水軍西上，非周年不達，外無軍援，一可圖也。

translations.literal: The navy going west cannot arrive in less than a full year, and there is no military aid from outside—this is the first reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: A fleet sailing west cannot arrive in less than a full year, and there is no outside military support. That is the first reason Shu can be taken.

sentences.zh: 益州頃經劉季連反叛，鄧元起攻圍，資儲散盡，倉庫空竭，今猶未復，兼民人喪膽，無復固守之意，二可圖也。

translations.literal: Yizhou not long ago suffered Liu Jilian's rebellion; Deng Yuanqi besieged it until stores were scattered and exhausted and the granaries emptied, and they have still not recovered; moreover the people have lost heart and no longer have the will to hold firm—this is the second reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou has only lately endured Liu Jilian's rebellion and Deng Yuanqi's siege, which emptied its stores and granaries, and it has not yet recovered. The people have lost heart and no longer mean to hold out. That is the second reason.

sentences.zh: 蕭淵藻是裙屐少年，[4]未洽治務，及至益州，便戮鄧元起、[5]曹亮宗，臨戎斬將，則是駕馭失方。

translations.literal: Xiao Yuanzao is a slipper-wearing youth, [4] unversed in governing affairs; as soon as he reached Yizhou he executed Deng Yuanqi [5] and Cao Liangzong; to behead generals on the eve of battle is to lose control of the chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yuanzao is a pampered young man [4] with no grasp of administration. As soon as he reached Yizhou he executed Deng Yuanqi [5] and Cao Liangzong. To kill generals on the eve of battle is to lose command of one's forces.

sentences.zh: 范國惠津渠退敗，鎖執在獄。

translations.literal: Fan Guohui was defeated at the Jinqu Canal and is shackled in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Guohui was defeated at the Jinqu Canal and is now shackled in prison.

sentences.zh: 今之所任，並非宿將重名，皆是左右少年而已，既不厭民望，多行殘暴，民心離解，三可圖也。

translations.literal: Those now in office are none of them veteran generals of great name; all are mere youthful attendants. They neither satisfy the people's hopes nor refrain from cruelty; popular hearts are divided and scattered—this is the third reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Those now in command are none of them seasoned generals of renown, only youthful favorites at court. They neither command popular respect nor refrain from cruelty, and the people's loyalty is breaking apart. That is the third reason.

sentences.zh: 蜀之所恃唯劍閣，今既克南安，已奪其險，據彼界內，三分已一。

translations.literal: What Shu relies on is only Jian'ge; now that Nan'an has been taken, its peril has already been seized, and within that border a third is already held.
translations.idiomatic: Shu relies on nothing but Jian'ge Pass. Now that Nan'an is taken, its strategic barrier is lost and a third of its territory within the border is already in our hands.

sentences.zh: 從南安向涪，方軌任意，前軍累破，後眾喪魂，四可圖也。

translations.literal: From Nan'an toward Fu the road is open at will; the vanguard has repeatedly been broken and the rear host has lost its spirit—this is the fourth reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: From Nan'an to Fu the road lies open. The enemy vanguard has been broken again and again and the rear ranks have lost heart. That is the fourth reason.

sentences.zh: 昔劉禪據一國之地，姜維為佐，鄧艾既出綿竹，彼即投降。

translations.literal: In the past Liu Shan held the territory of a whole state with Jiang Wei as his aide; once Deng Ai had come out of Mianzhu, they at once surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Liu Shan held an entire kingdom with Jiang Wei as his chief aide, yet once Deng Ai emerged from Mianzhu they surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅之世，楊安、朱彤三月取漢中，四月至涪城，兵未及州，仲孫逃命。

translations.literal: In the time of Fu Jian, Yang An and Zhu Tong took Hanzhong in the third month and reached Fucheng in the fourth; the army had not yet reached the provincial capital when Zhongsun fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian, Yang An and Zhu Tong took Hanzhong in the third month and reached Fucheng in the fourth. The army had not yet reached the provincial capital when Zhongsun fled for his life.

sentences.zh: 桓溫西征，不旬月而平。

translations.literal: Huan Wen's western expedition pacified it in less than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's western expedition pacified Shu in less than ten days.

sentences.zh: 蜀地昔來恒多不守。

translations.literal: The land of Shu from of old has constantly been hard to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Shu has always been difficult to defend.

sentences.zh: 況淵藻是蕭衍兄子，骨肉至親，若其逃亡，當無死理。

translations.literal: Moreover Yuanzao is Xiao Yan's elder brother's son, flesh and bone in the closest kinship; if he flees, there should be no reason for him to live.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yuanzao is Xiao Yan's own nephew, his closest kin. If he flees, his uncle will surely have him put to death.

sentences.zh: 脫軍克涪城，淵藻復何宜城中坐而受困？

translations.literal: If the army takes Fucheng, how would it be fitting for Yuanzao to sit in the city and await encirclement?
translations.idiomatic: If our army takes Fucheng, how can Yuanzao simply sit in the city and wait to be trapped?

sentences.zh: 若其出鬬，庸蜀之卒唯便刀矟，弓箭至少，假有遙射，弗至傷人，五可圖也。

translations.literal: If he comes out to fight, the soldiers of Yong and Shu are skilled only with blade and spear; bows and arrows are very few—even if they shoot from afar, they will not reach to wound a man—this is the fifth reason it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: If he comes out to fight, the soldiers of Shu are handy only with blade and spear; they have very few bows and arrows, and even if they shoot from a distance they will hardly wound anyone. That is the fifth reason.

sentences.zh: 臣聞乘機而動，武之善經；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that to move when the opportunity arises is the excellent constant of warfare;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to strike when opportunity offers is the supreme principle of war;

sentences.zh: 攻昧侮亡，春秋明義。

translations.literal: to attack the benighted and despise the perishing is the clear principle of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: and to attack the benighted and despise a state in its death throes is the clear teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 未有捨干戚而康時，不征伐而混一。

translations.literal: never yet has the age been made tranquil by laying aside arms and shields, or the realm unified without campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has an age been pacified by laying aside arms, or the realm unified without campaigning.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下纂武文之業，當必世之期，跨中州之饒，兼甲兵之盛，清蕩天區，在於今矣。

translations.literal: I bow to consider that Your Majesty continues the enterprise of King Wu and King Wen, meets the term of assured succession, spans the richness of the central provinces, and combines the fullness of armored troops— to sweep clean the heavenly regions is a matter for this very day.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty continues the work of King Wu and King Wen, stands at the destined hour of assured succession, commands the wealth of the central provinces and the strength of armored hosts—to sweep the realm clean is a task for this very day.

sentences.zh: 是以踐極之初，壽春馳款；

translations.literal: Therefore at the beginning of your accession Shouchun came offering allegiance;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of your reign Shouchun offered its allegiance;

sentences.zh: 先歲命將，義陽克闢。

translations.literal: the year before you ordered generals forth and Yiyang was taken and opened.
translations.idiomatic: the year before last you sent generals forth and Yiyang was conquered.

sentences.zh: 淮外謐以風清，荊沔於焉肅晏。

translations.literal: Beyond the Huai all was tranquil as the wind was clear; Jing and Mian were thereby solemn and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Huai all was tranquil; along the Jing and Mian the borders grew calm.

sentences.zh: 方欲偃甲息兵，候機而動，而天贊休明，時來斯速，雖欲靖戎，理不獲已。

translations.literal: Just as you wished to rest the armor and still the weapons and await the moment to move, Heaven has aided your glorious brightness and the time has come with such speed that though you wish to quiet warfare, reason will not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: You had just wished to rest the armies and await the right moment, yet Heaven favors your glorious rule and the hour has come with such speed that, though you would prefer peace, necessity will not permit it.

sentences.zh: 至使道遷歸誠，漢境佇拔。

translations.literal: It has even brought Daoyian's return in sincerity and Han territory waiting to be drawn up.
translations.idiomatic: It has even brought Daoyian's surrender and Han territory waiting to be taken.

sentences.zh: 臣以不才，屬當戎寄，內省文吏，不以軍謀自許，指臨漢中，惟規保疆守界。

translations.literal: Your subject, lacking talent, has been entrusted with military charge; inwardly considering himself a clerk, he does not claim military counsel for himself; facing Hanzhong, he only planned to guard the borders and hold the boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: I, lacking talent, have been entrusted with military command. Knowing myself to be a clerk at heart, I did not presume on military strategy; facing Hanzhong I intended only to secure the borders.

sentences.zh: 事屬艱途，東西寇竊，上憑國威，下仗將士，邊帥用命，頻有薄捷。

translations.literal: The affair belonged to a hard road; bandits raided east and west; above he relied on the state's majesty, below on officers and soldiers; frontier commanders obeyed orders and there were frequent modest victories.
translations.idiomatic: The task proved arduous. Raiders struck east and west. Relying above on the state's majesty and below on officers and men, the frontier commanders obeyed orders and we won frequent minor victories.

sentences.zh: 藉勢乘威，經度大劍，既克南安，據彼要險，前軍長邁，已至梓潼，新化之民，翻然懷惠，瞻望涪益，旦夕可屠。

translations.literal: Borrowing momentum and riding prestige, he traversed the Great Sword Pass; having taken Nan'an he held their strategic peril; the vanguard marched far and had already reached Zitong; the newly transformed people suddenly turned with favor; gazing toward Fu and Yi, they could be slaughtered within the day.
translations.idiomatic: Riding our momentum we crossed the Great Sword Pass, took Nan'an, and held the strategic heights. The vanguard has marched far and reached Zitong. The newly submitted people have turned to us in goodwill. Fu and Yi lie before us and may fall at any moment.

sentences.zh: 正以兵少糧匱，未宜前出。

translations.literal: It is precisely because troops are few and grain scarce that it is not yet fitting to advance.
translations.idiomatic: It is precisely because our troops are few and grain short that we ought not advance yet.

sentences.zh: 為爾稽緩，懼失民心，則更為寇。

translations.literal: For this reason delay and slowness fear losing the people's hearts, and then they would again become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if we delay for that reason we risk losing the people's hearts, and they will turn to raiding again.

sentences.zh: 今若不取，後圖便難，輒率愚管，庶幾殄克，如其無功，分受憲坐。

translations.literal: If we do not take it now, later plans will be difficult; I rashly lead my foolish counsel, hoping perhaps for complete destruction of the enemy; if there is no success, let me share in punishment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not take it now, later action will be far harder. I venture this humble counsel in hope of complete victory. If I fail, let me bear my share of punishment under the law.

sentences.zh: 且益州殷實，戶餘十萬，比壽春、義陽三倍非匹，可乘可利，實在于茲。

translations.literal: Moreover Yizhou is rich and solid, with more than a hundred thousand households—compared with Shouchun and Yiyang, three times and not comparable; what may be seized and what may profit truly lie here.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yizhou is rich and populous, with more than a hundred thousand households—three times the prize of Shouchun or Yiyang. The gain to be seized lies here.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷志存保民，未欲經略，臣之在此，便為無事，乞歸侍養，微展烏鳥。

translations.literal: If the court's will is to preserve the people and it does not yet wish for grand strategy, then your subject's presence here is without affair; I beg to return and attend my parents, slightly to fulfill the crow's filial turn.
translations.idiomatic: If the court wishes only to protect the people and has no mind for conquest, then I have no further business here. I beg leave to return home and care for my parents, however briefly, in filial duty.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「若賊敢闚𨵦，觀機翦撲；

translations.literal: An edict said: "If the enemy dares peer at the passes, watch the moment and cut them down;
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "If the enemy dares threaten the passes, watch for the moment and strike them down;

sentences.zh: 如其無也，則安民保境，以悅邊心。

translations.literal: if they do not, then settle the people and guard the borders to please the hearts of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: if they do not, then settle the people and secure the borders to win the frontier's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 子蜀之舉，更聽後敕。

translations.literal: Your campaign into Shu—await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: Your campaign into Shu must await further orders.

sentences.zh: 方將席卷岷蜀，電掃西南，何得辭以戀親，中途告退！

translations.literal: We are just about to roll up Min and Shu like a mat and sweep the southwest like lightning—how can you plead love of kin and announce withdrawal midway!
translations.idiomatic: We are about to roll up Min and Shu and sweep the southwest like lightning—how can you plead devotion to your parents and withdraw midway!

sentences.zh: 宜勗令圖，務申高略。

translations.literal: You should urge your plans forward and strive to carry out the lofty strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Press on with your plans and carry out the grand strategy."

sentences.zh: 」巒又表曰：

translations.literal: " Luan memorialized again:
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 昔鄧艾、鍾會率十八萬眾，傾中國資給，裁得平蜀，所以然者，鬬實力故也。

translations.literal: In the past Deng Ai and Zhong Hui led one hundred eighty thousand men and exhausted the resources of the central state to supply them, and only just pacified Shu; the reason was that they fought with solid strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Deng Ai and Zhong Hui led one hundred eighty thousand men and drained the central state's resources before they barely pacified Shu, because they fought with overwhelming force.

sentences.zh: 況臣才絕古人，智勇又闕，復何宜請二萬之眾而希平蜀？

translations.literal: How much less can your subject, whose talent surpasses the ancients yet whose wisdom and courage are lacking, again be fit to ask for twenty thousand men and hope to pacify Shu?
translations.idiomatic: How much less am I—whose talent falls far short of the ancients and whose wisdom and courage are wanting—fit to ask for twenty thousand men and hope to pacify Shu?

sentences.zh: 所以敢者，正以據得要險，士民慕義，此往則易，彼來則難，任力而行，理有可克。

translations.literal: The reason I dare is precisely that we hold the key passes and perilous terrain, and officials and commoners honor righteousness—going there is easy, coming here is difficult; acting with force, reason holds that we can conquer.
translations.idiomatic: I dare propose this because we hold the strategic passes and rugged ground, and gentry and people alike look to us for justice. It is easy for us to advance there and hard for them to come here; if we bring our strength to bear, victory is within reason.

sentences.zh: 今王足前進，已逼涪城，脫得涪城，則益州便是成擒之物，但得之有早晚耳。

translations.literal: Now Wang Zu's advance has already pressed upon Fucheng; if Fucheng is taken, then Yizhou is simply something already captured—it is only a matter of sooner or later.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Zu has already advanced as far as Fucheng. Once Fucheng falls, Yizhou is as good as ours—it is only a question of whether we take it sooner or later.

sentences.zh: 且梓潼已附，民戶數萬，朝廷豈得不守之也？

translations.literal: Moreover, Zitong has already submitted, with tens of thousands of households—how can the court fail to defend it?
translations.idiomatic: Zitong has already surrendered, with tens of thousands of households. How can the court leave it undefended?

sentences.zh: 若守也，直保境之兵則已一萬，臣今請二萬伍千，所增無幾。

translations.literal: If it is defended, the troops guarding the border alone would already be ten thousand; I now request twenty-five thousand—the increase is not much.
translations.idiomatic: To hold it would take ten thousand men on the frontier alone. I am asking for only twenty-five thousand—a modest addition.

sentences.zh: 又劍閣天險，古來所稱，張載銘云：「世亂則逆，世清斯順。

translations.literal: Again, Jian'ge is heaven's peril, famed since antiquity; Zhang Zai's inscription says: "When the age is in turmoil, then it turns against you; when the age is pure, then it yields.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'ge, too, is nature's fortress, renowned since ancient times. As Zhang Zai's inscription puts it: "In chaotic times it turns hostile; in orderly times it opens itself.

sentences.zh: 」此之一言，良可惜矣。

translations.literal: " This one saying—how truly regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: " That line alone is deeply lamentable.

sentences.zh: 臣誠知征戎危事，不易可為，自軍度劍閣以來，鬢髮中白，憂慮戰懼，寧可一日為心。

translations.literal: Your subject truly knows that campaigning is a perilous affair, not easily done; since the army crossed Jian'ge, half the hair at my temples has turned white—worry and fear of battle, could I set them aside for even a day?
translations.idiomatic: I know full well that war is perilous and not lightly undertaken. Since our troops crossed Jian'ge, my temples have gone half gray with worry and dread of battle—not for a single day have I been free of it.

sentences.zh: 所以勉強者，既得此地而自退不守，恐辜先皇之恩遇，負陛下之爵祿，是以孜孜，頻有陳請。

translations.literal: The reason I force myself on is that having gained this territory yet withdrawing and not holding it, I fear I would fail the late emperor's favor and betray Your Majesty's rank and stipend; therefore I have been diligent and repeatedly submitted petitions.
translations.idiomatic: I press on only because to take this ground and then abandon it would betray the late emperor's kindness and Your Majesty's trust and pay. That is why I have kept at it and petitioned again and again.

sentences.zh: 且臣之意算，正欲先圖涪城，以漸而進。

translations.literal: Moreover, my intended plan is precisely to first aim at Fucheng and advance by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: My plan is to take Fucheng first and advance step by step.

sentences.zh: 若克涪城，便是中分益州之地，斷水陸之衝，彼外無援軍，孤城自守，復何能持久哉！

translations.literal: If Fucheng is taken, it would mean splitting Yizhou in half, cutting the land-and-water thoroughfare; with no relief armies outside, a lone city holding on—how could it last long!
translations.idiomatic: Once Fucheng falls, we cut Yizhou in half and sever their land and water routes. Cut off from relief, how long can a lone citadel stand?

sentences.zh: 臣今欲使軍軍相次，聲勢連接，先作萬全之計，然後圖彼，得之則大克，不得則自全。

translations.literal: Your subject now wishes to have armies follow one another in succession, momentum linked in chain, first making a plan of complete security, then aiming at them—if obtained, then a great victory; if not, then preserving ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: I propose to march our forces in close succession, keeping our strength continuous. We must first secure every contingency, then strike. Success would mean a great conquest; failure would still leave us intact.

sentences.zh: 又巴西、南鄭相離一千四百，去州迢遞，恒多生動。

translations.literal: Again, Ba and Nanzheng are fourteen hundred li apart, far from the provincial capital, and unrest constantly arises.
translations.idiomatic: Ba and Nanzheng lie fourteen hundred li apart from each other and far from the provincial seat—trouble flares there constantly.

sentences.zh: 昔在南之日，以其統綰勢難，故增立巴州，鎮靜夷獠，梁州藉利，因而表罷。

translations.literal: Formerly, during the days in the south, because unified control was difficult, therefore Ba Province was additionally established to pacify the barbarians and Liao; Liang Province benefited thereby, and consequently memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: When we held the south, governance there was unwieldy, so Ba Province was established to pacify the tribal peoples. Liang Province profited from the arrangement and then petitioned to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 彼土民望，嚴、蒲、何、楊，非唯五三，族落雖在山居，而多有豪右，文學箋啟，往往可觀，冠帶風流，亦為不少。

translations.literal: The local worthies of that land—the Yan, Pu, He, and Yang clans, and not only five or three of them—though their settlements dwell in the mountains, many are powerful magnates; their literary memorials are often impressive, and men of culture and refinement are also not a few.
translations.idiomatic: The leading families of that region—the Yan, Pu, He, and Yang clans among many others—live in mountain settlements yet include numerous powerful magnates. Their literary petitions are often impressive, and cultured gentlemen are plentiful as well.

sentences.zh: 但以去州既遠，不能仕進，至於州綱，無由厠迹。

translations.literal: But because they are far from the provincial capital, they cannot advance in office; as for the provincial leadership, there is no way to gain a place.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because they are so far from the capital, they cannot rise in office and have no path into provincial leadership.

sentences.zh: 巴境民豪，便是無梁州之分，是以鬱怏，多生動靜。

translations.literal: The magnates of Ba territory thus had no share of Liang Province; therefore they were resentful, and much unrest arose.
translations.idiomatic: The local elites of Ba felt cut off from Liang Province, bred resentment, and stirred up trouble.

sentences.zh: 比建議之始，[6]嚴玄思自號巴州刺史，克城以來，仍使行事。

translations.literal: At the start of this proposal, [6] Yan Xuansi styled himself Prefect of Ba Province; since taking the city, he has continued to act in that capacity.
translations.idiomatic: When this plan was first raised, [6] Yan Xuansi proclaimed himself Prefect of Ba Province and has held power there ever since the city was taken.

sentences.zh: 巴西廣袤一千，戶餘四萬，若彼立州，鎮攝華獠，則大帖民情。

translations.literal: Ba extends a thousand li, with more than forty thousand households; if a province were established there to control the Chinese and Liao, then the people's sentiments would be greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ba spans a thousand li with more than forty thousand households. Establishing a province there to govern both Han settlers and tribal peoples would greatly placate the populace.

sentences.zh: 從墊江已還，不復勞征，自為國有。

translations.literal: From Dianjiang eastward, no further expeditions would be needed—it would be the state's own territory.
translations.idiomatic: From Dianjiang eastward, no further campaigns would be needed—the land would be securely ours.

sentences.zh: 世宗不從。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu refused.

sentences.zh: 又王足於涪城輒還，遂不定蜀。

translations.literal: Again, Wang Zu abruptly returned at Fucheng, and thus Shu was not stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Zu withdrew suddenly from Fucheng, and the conquest of Shu was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 巒既克巴西，遣軍主李仲遷守之。

translations.literal: Luan, having taken Ba, dispatched the military commander Li Zhongqian to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: After Luan conquered Ba, he sent the garrison commander Li Zhongqian to hold it.

sentences.zh: 仲遷得蕭衍將張法養女，有美色，甚惑之。

translations.literal: Zhongqian obtained the daughter of Xiao Yan's general Zhang Fayang—she had fine beauty, and he was greatly infatuated with her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqian took the daughter of Xiao Yan's general Zhang Fayang—a woman of striking beauty—and became utterly smitten.

sentences.zh: 散費兵儲，專心酒色，公事諮承，無能見者。

translations.literal: He squandered military stores, devoted himself entirely to wine and women; public business consultation and reporting—none could reach him.
translations.idiomatic: He squandered military supplies on wine and women, and no official business could reach him.

sentences.zh: 巒忿之切齒，仲遷懼，謀叛，城人斬其首，以城降衍將譙希遠，巴西遂沒。

translations.literal: Luan gnashed his teeth in rage at him; Zhongqian feared and plotted rebellion; the city's people cut off his head and surrendered the city to Xiao Yan's general Qiao Xiyuan—Ba was then lost.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was furious. Zhongqian, fearing for his life, plotted rebellion, but the townspeople beheaded him and surrendered to Xiao Yan's general Qiao Xiyuan. Ba was lost.

sentences.zh: 武興氐楊集起等反叛，巒遣統軍傅豎眼討平之，語在豎眼傳。

translations.literal: The Di of Wuxing, Yang Jiqing and others, rebelled; Luan dispatched the commander Fu Shuyan to suppress and pacify them—the account is in Shuyan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Jiqing of Wuxing and others rose in rebellion. Luan sent Commander Fu Shuyan to put them down; the full account appears in Shuyan's biography.

sentences.zh: 巒之初至漢中，從容風雅，接豪右以禮，撫細民以惠。

translations.literal: When Luan first arrived in Hanzhong, he was easy and refined in manner, received magnates with ceremony, and soothed common folk with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan first arrived in Hanzhong, he carried himself with easy grace, treated local elites with courtesy, and dealt kindly with the common people.

sentences.zh: 歲餘之後，頗因百姓去就，誅滅齊民，藉為奴婢者二百餘口，兼商販聚歛，清論鄙之。

translations.literal: After a year or more, he rather often on the basis of people's leaving or staying executed and wiped out common households, seizing more than two hundred persons as slaves and maidservants; moreover he engaged in trade and hoarded wealth—men of clear judgment despised him.
translations.idiomatic: After a year, he began executing ordinary families over questions of loyalty, enslaving more than two hundred people, and profiteering through trade. Men of reputation held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 徵授度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍遣兵侵軼徐兗，緣邊鎮戍相繼陷沒，朝廷憂之，乃以巒為使持節、都督東討諸軍事、安東將軍，尚書如故。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Yan sent troops to raid Xu and Yan; frontier garrisons fell one after another; the court was troubled by this, and thereupon appointed Luan as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of All Eastern Campaign Forces, General Who Pacifies the East, retaining his ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan's forces raided Xu and Yan and frontier garrisons fell in succession, the court grew alarmed and appointed Luan Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Eastern Expeditionary Forces, and General Who Pacifies the East, while retaining his post as minister.

sentences.zh: 世宗勞遣巒於東堂曰：「蕭衍寇邊，旬朔滋甚，諸軍舛互，規致連戍陷沒。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu saw Luan off with encouragement at the Eastern Hall, saying: "Xiao Yan raids the frontier; within ten days and a month it grows worse; the armies are at cross purposes, intending to cause successive garrisons to fall.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Hall, Emperor Xuanwu bid Luan farewell with these words: "Xiao Yan ravages our borders day by day. Our armies clash with one another and our garrisons fall one after another.

sentences.zh: 宋魯之民尤罹湯炭。

translations.literal: The people of Song and Lu especially suffer boiling water and burning coals.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Song and Lu suffer most cruelly.

sentences.zh: 誠知將軍旋京未久，膝下難違，然東南之寄，非將軍莫可。

translations.literal: I truly know the general has returned to the capital not long and finds it hard to leave parents' knees; yet the trust placed in the southeast—none but the general can bear it.
translations.idiomatic: I know you have only lately returned to the capital and find it hard to leave your parents, yet the southeast has no one else to trust but you.

sentences.zh: 將軍其勉建殊績，以稱朕懷，自古忠臣亦非無孝也。

translations.literal: General, exert yourself to establish extraordinary merit, to match my hopes—from antiquity loyal ministers too have not been without filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Strive for outstanding achievement to meet my expectations. Loyal ministers have never lacked filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 」巒對曰：「賊雖送死連城，犬羊眾盛，然逆順理殊，滅當無遠。

translations.literal: " Luan replied: "Though the rebels stake city after city in a death rush, dogs and sheep are many and strong, yet the righteous and rebellious differ in principle—their destruction surely cannot be far.
translations.idiomatic: " Luan replied, "Though the rebels hold city after city and their numbers are great as a flock of beasts, the righteous and the rebellious stand on opposite grounds—their destruction cannot be far off.

sentences.zh: 況臣仗陛下之神算，奉律以摧之，平殄之期可指辰而待，願陛下勿以東南為慮。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject relies on Your Majesty's divine calculation, upholds the law to crush them—the day of total pacification can be awaited by pointing to the time; I pray Your Majesty not take the southeast as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: And with Your Majesty's wise guidance and proper discipline, their annihilation is near at hand. I beg Your Majesty not to worry about the southeast.

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「漢祖有云『金吾擊郾，吾無憂矣』，今將軍董戎，朕何慮哉。」

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanwu said: "Han the Ancestor said, 'The Golden Guard strikes Ying—I have no worry'; now the general directs the army—what worry have I!"
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu said, "When Han the Founder's forces struck Ying, he said he had no further worries. With you commanding our armies, what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭衍輔國將軍蕭及先率眾二萬，寇陷固城；

translations.literal: Previously, Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Xiao Jixian led twenty thousand men and raided, capturing Gucheng;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Yan's general Xiao Jixian had led twenty thousand men and captured Gucheng;

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍魯顯文、驍騎將軍相文玉等率眾一萬，屯於孤山；

translations.literal: Champion General Lu Xianwen, Valiant Cavalry General Xiang Wenyu and others led ten thousand men and encamped at Gushan;
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Lu Xianwen and Valiant Cavalry General Xiang Wenyu encamped ten thousand men on Lone Mountain;

sentences.zh: [7]衍將角念等率眾一萬，擾亂龜蒙，土民從逆，十室而五。

translations.literal: [7] Xiao Yan's general Jiao Nian and others led ten thousand men, disturbing Gui and Meng; local people followed the rebels—five in ten households.
translations.idiomatic: [7] Xiao Yan's general Jiao Nian and others led ten thousand men to ravage the Gui and Meng region, where half the local households joined the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 巒遣統軍樊魯討文玉，別將元恒攻固城，統軍畢祖朽討角念。

translations.literal: Luan dispatched Commander Fan Lu to attack Wenyu, a separate general Yuan Heng to assault Gucheng, and Commander Bi Zuxiu to attack Jiao Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Luan sent Commander Fan Lu against Wenyu, Yuan Heng against Gucheng, and Commander Bi Zuxiu against Jiao Nian.

sentences.zh: 樊魯大破文玉等，追奔八十餘里，斬首四千餘級。

translations.literal: Fan Lu greatly defeated Wenyu and the others, pursued the fleeing enemy eighty-odd li, and beheaded more than four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Lu routed Wenyu's forces, pursued them eighty li, and took more than four thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 元恒又破固城，畢祖朽復破念等，兗州悉平。

translations.literal: Yuan Heng again captured Gucheng; Bi Zuxiu again defeated Nian and the others; Yan Province was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Heng retook Gucheng, Bi Zuxiu defeated Jiao Nian, and Yan Province was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 巒破賊將藍懷恭於睢口，進圍宿豫。

translations.literal: Luan defeated the rebel general Lan Huaigong at Suikou and advanced to besiege Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: Luan defeated the rebel general Lan Huaigong at Suikou and marched to besiege Suyu.

sentences.zh: 而懷恭等復於清南造城，[8]規斷水陸之路。

translations.literal: But Huaigong and the others again built a fortress at Qingnan, [8] intending to cut the land-and-water routes.
translations.idiomatic: Huaigong then built a fortress at Qingnan, [8] aiming to sever our land and water lines of communication.

sentences.zh: 巒身率諸軍，自水南而進，遣平南將軍楊大眼從北逼之，統軍劉思祖等夾水造筏，燒其船舫。

translations.literal: Luan personally led the armies, advancing from south of the water; he dispatched General Who Pacifies the South Yang Dayan to press from the north; Commanders Liu Sizu and others built rafts on both sides of the water and burned their ships.
translations.idiomatic: Luan personally led his forces south across the water while General Yang Dayan pressed from the north. Liu Sizu and others built rafts on both banks and burned the enemy fleet.

sentences.zh: 眾軍齊進，拔柵填塹，登其城。

translations.literal: The armies advanced together, pulled up palisades, filled moats, and mounted their wall.
translations.idiomatic: The armies advanced together, tore down palisades, filled the moats, and stormed the walls.

sentences.zh: 火起中流，四面俱擊，仍陷賊城，俘斬數萬。

translations.literal: Fire rose midstream; all sides struck together; they then captured the rebel fortress, capturing and slaying tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Fires blazed on the water as attacks converged from every side. The rebel fortress fell, with tens of thousands killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 在陳別斬懷恭，擒其列侯、列將、直閤、直後三十餘人，俘斬一萬。

translations.literal: At Chen, separately beheaded Huaigong, captured more than thirty of their ranked marquises, ranked generals, palace attendants, and rear attendants; captured and slayed ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In battle they beheaded Huaigong and captured more than thirty of his nobles, generals, and staff officers, killing or capturing ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 宿豫既平，蕭昞亦於淮陽退走，二戍獲米四十餘萬石。

translations.literal: Suyu having been pacified, Xiao Bing also retreated at Huaiyang; from the two garrisons more than four hundred thousand shi of grain were seized.
translations.idiomatic: With Suyu pacified, Xiao Bing withdrew from Huaiyang as well. The two garrisons yielded more than four hundred thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 世宗賜巒璽書曰：「知大龕醜虜，威振賊庭，淮外霧披，徐方卷壒，王略遠恢，混一維始，公私慶泰，何快如之！

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu granted Luan an imperial letter, saying: "Knowing the great abyss of ugly barbarians, your might shakes the rebel court; beyond the Huai the mist is parted, Xu region rolls up its dust; the royal strategy extends far, unification begins—public and private rejoice in peace—what joy like this!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu sent Luan an imperial letter: "You have crushed the enemy's stronghold and shaken their court. Beyond the Huai the fog has lifted; in Xu the dust of war settles. Our royal design reaches far and unification begins—what greater joy for throne and people alike!

sentences.zh: 賊衍此舉，實為傾國。

translations.literal: The rebel Yan's this move truly is staking the nation.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign of the rebel Xiao Yan truly risked his entire state.

sentences.zh: 比者宿豫陷歿，淮陽嬰城，凶狡侜張，規抗王旅。

translations.literal: Recently Suyu fell and was lost, Huaiyang clung to its walls—the vicious and cunning spread deception, intending to resist the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Suyu had fallen and Huaiyang had held out, while the enemy's cunning leaders schemed to resist the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 將軍忠規協著，火烈霜摧，電動岱陰，風掃沂嶧，遂令逋誅之寇，一朝殲夷；

translations.literal: General, your loyal counsel shines in agreement—fire fierce, frost shattering, lightning moving at Dai's foot, wind sweeping Yi and Yi—thus causing the long-fugitive rebels, in one morning to be annihilated;
translations.idiomatic: Through your steadfast counsel and coordinated action—fierce as fire, swift as frost, lightning at the foot of Mount Tai, wind sweeping through Yi and Yi—you annihilated these long-elusive rebels in a single morning;

sentences.zh: 元鯨大憝，千里折首。

translations.literal: The chief whale, great villain—its head broken a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: the great whale of villainy beheaded a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 殊勳茂捷，自古莫二。

translations.literal: Extraordinary merit, flourishing victory—from antiquity none second.
translations.idiomatic: Such extraordinary merit and brilliant victory are unmatched since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 但揚區未安，餘燼宜盪，乘勝掎角，勢不可遺。

translations.literal: But the Yang region is not yet settled; remaining embers should be swept; riding victory in pincer—momentum must not be wasted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Yang region is not secure, and lingering embers must be stamped out. You must press the advantage in concert—this momentum cannot be squandered.

sentences.zh: 便可率厲三軍，因時經略，申威東南，清彼江介，忘此仍勞，用圖永逸，進退規度，委之高算。

translations.literal: Then you may lead and encourage the three armies, seize the season to strategize, extend might to the southeast, clear their Jiang frontier—forget this continuing toil, use it to seek lasting ease; advance and retreat measures, entrust to your high calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Lead the three armies, exploit the moment, extend our power into the southeast, and clear the Yangtze frontier. Accept present hardship for lasting peace. As for the conduct of the campaign, I leave all to your judgment.

sentences.zh: 」又詔巒曰：「淮陽、宿豫雖已清復，梁城之賊，猶敢聚結，事宜乘勝，并勢摧殄。

translations.literal: " Again he edicted to Luan: "Huaiyang and Suyu though already cleared and recovered, the rebels at Liangcheng still dare to gather—affairs demand riding victory, combining momentum to crush and exterminate.
translations.idiomatic: " A further edict read: "Though Huaiyang and Suyu are restored, the rebels at Liangcheng still gather. Strike while victory is fresh and destroy them with combined force.

sentences.zh: 可率二萬之眾渡淮，與征南掎角，以圖進取之計。」

translations.literal: You may lead twenty thousand men to cross the Huai, coordinate with the southern expedition in pincer, to devise a plan of advance and seizure."
translations.idiomatic: Cross the Huai with twenty thousand men and coordinate with the southern expeditionary force to press the advance."

sentences.zh: 及梁城賊走，中山王英乘勝攻鍾離，又詔巒帥眾會之。

translations.literal: When the Liangcheng rebels fled, Prince of Zhongshan Ying pursued victory to attack Zhongli; again Luan was edicted to lead troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liangcheng rebels fled, Prince Ying of Zhongshan pressed the attack on Zhongli, and Luan was ordered to bring his forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 巒表曰：「奉被詔旨，令臣濟淮與征南掎角，乘勝長驅，實是其會。

translations.literal: Luan memorialized: "I have received the edict, ordering your subject to cross the Huai and coordinate with the southern expedition in pincer, riding victory in long drive—truly this is the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized: "I have received Your Majesty's order to cross the Huai and coordinate with the southern expedition, riding our victory in a long advance—a true opportunity.

sentences.zh: 但愚懷所量，竊有未盡。

translations.literal: But what my foolish heart measures, I privately have not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my humble judgment still harbors reservations.

sentences.zh: 夫圖南因於積風，伐國在於資給，用兵治戎，須先計校。

translations.literal: To aim south depends on accumulated wind; conquering a state depends on supplies; employing troops and managing armies requires first calculating and comparing.
translations.idiomatic: Flight to the south depends on steady wind; conquest depends on supply. War demands careful reckoning beforehand.

sentences.zh: 非可抑為必勝，[9]幸其無能。

translations.literal: One cannot suppress reality into assured victory, [9] hoping in their incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: One cannot assume certain victory [9] and count on the enemy's incompetence.

sentences.zh: 若欲掠地誅民，必應萬勝；

translations.literal: If one wishes to plunder land and execute the people, one must have ten-thousand-fold victory;
translations.idiomatic: To ravage the countryside and slaughter the people, one must be utterly assured of victory;

sentences.zh: 如欲攻城取邑，未見其果。

translations.literal: If one wishes to assault cities and take towns, I do not see the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: to assault cities and seize towns, I see no promise of success.

sentences.zh: 得之則所益未幾，不獲則虧損必大。

translations.literal: If obtained, the gain would be little; if not obtained, the loss would surely be great.
translations.idiomatic: Success would bring little gain; failure would bring great loss.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍傾竭江東，為今歲之舉，疲兵喪眾，大敗而還，君臣失計，取笑天下。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan exhausted Jiangdong for this year's campaign; weary troops, lost masses, great defeat and return—lord and ministers lost their reckoning, becoming ridicule under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan poured all of Jiangdong into this year's campaign, only to return with exhausted armies and heavy losses—a failure that has made him and his court a laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 雖野戰非人敵，守城足有餘，今雖攻之，未易可克。

translations.literal: Though in field battle they are no match for others, for holding cities they have more than enough; now though we attack, it is not easily taken.
translations.idiomatic: They may be weak in the field, but they can defend cities well enough. An assault now would not be easily won.

sentences.zh: 又廣陵懸遠，去江四十里，鍾離、淮陰介在淮外，假其歸順而來，猶恐無糧艱守，況加攻討，勞兵士乎？

translations.literal: Again, Guangling hangs distant, forty li from the Jiang; Zhongli and Huaiyin lie beyond the Huai—suppose they submitted and came over, still one fears no grain and difficult holding; how much more adding assault and attack, toiling the soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: Guangling lies far away, forty li from the Yangtze; Zhongli and Huaiyin stand beyond the Huai. Even if they surrendered willingly, holding them without adequate grain would be hard—how much harder to take them by force and wear out our troops?

sentences.zh: 且征南軍士從戎二時，疲弊死病，量可知已。

translations.literal: Moreover the southern expedition's soldiers have campaigned two seasons—exhausted, worn, dead and sick—the measure can be known.
translations.idiomatic: The southern expeditionary forces have campaigned for two seasons; their exhaustion, sickness, and death are plain to see.

sentences.zh: 雖有乘勝之資，懼無遠用之力。

translations.literal: Though having the resource of riding victory, I fear having no strength for distant use.
translations.idiomatic: We may have the momentum of victory, but I fear we lack the strength for a distant campaign.

sentences.zh: 若臣之愚見，謂宜修復舊戍，牢實邊方，息養中州，擬之後舉。

translations.literal: If your subject's foolish view, I say we should repair and restore old garrisons, solidify the frontier, rest and nurture the central provinces, plan for a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, we should repair the old garrisons, strengthen the frontier, let the heartland recover, and plan a later offensive.

sentences.zh: 又江東之釁，不患久無，畜力待機，謂為勝計。

translations.literal: Again, Jiangdong's provocations—one need not worry they will not come again soon; storing strength awaiting opportunity—I call this the winning plan.
translations.idiomatic: Trouble from Jiangdong will surely come again. To husband our strength and await the right moment is the wiser strategy.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「濟淮掎角，事如前敕，何容猶爾磐桓，方有此請！

translations.literal: " The edict said: "Crossing the Huai in pincer—the matter is as in the previous command—how can you still thus linger, and now make this request!
translations.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "Cross the Huai and coordinate as previously ordered. How dare you still hesitate and petition thus!

sentences.zh: 可速進軍，經略之宜聽征南至要。」

translations.literal: Quickly advance the army; strategic measures—listen to the southern expedition's essential judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Advance at once. As for operational details, defer to the southern expeditionary commander."

sentences.zh: 巒又表曰：「蕭衍侵境，久勞王師，今者奔走，實除邊患，斯由靈贊皇魏，天敗寇豎，非臣等弱劣所能克勝。

translations.literal: Luan again memorialized: "Xiao Yan invaded the frontier, long tiring the royal army; now they flee in disarray—truly removing the border peril. This is by the numinous aid of Great Wei, heaven defeating the rebel rabble—not something your subject and others, weak and inferior, could conquer by victory.
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized again: "Xiao Yan's invasion long taxed the imperial armies. His flight has truly lifted the border threat—but this victory came through divine favor for Great Wei and heaven's judgment on the rebels, not through any merit of ours.

sentences.zh: 若臣之愚見，今正宜修復邊鎮，俟之後動。

translations.literal: If your subject's foolish view, now precisely we should repair and restore frontier garrisons, await later action.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, we should now repair the frontier garrisons and wait for a better opportunity.

sentences.zh: 且蕭衍尚在，凶身未除，螳蜋之志，何能自息。

translations.literal: Moreover Xiao Yan still lives, the vicious body not yet removed—the mantis's ambition—how can it rest of itself?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan yet lives and his evil is unabated. A mantis's ambition does not die of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 唯應廣備以待其來，實不宜勞師遠入，自取疲困。

translations.literal: Only we should broadly prepare to await their coming; truly it is not fitting to toil the army in distant entry, bringing exhaustion on ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: We should fortify our defenses and await his next move—not wear ourselves out on a distant expedition.

sentences.zh: 今中山進軍鍾離，實所未解，若能為得失之計，不顧萬全，直襲廣陵，入其內地，出其不備，或未可知。

translations.literal: Now Zhongshan advancing on Zhongli—truly I do not understand; if one could make a reckoning of gain and loss, disregard complete security, directly strike Guangling, enter their inner lands, catch them unprepared—perhaps it might bear some logic.
translations.idiomatic: I do not understand the advance on Zhongli. If one weighed costs against gains, abandoned every safeguard, and struck straight at Guangling deep in enemy territory by surprise—perhaps that might at least make some sense.

sentences.zh: 正欲屯兵，蕭密餘軍猶自在彼；

translations.literal: Just when one wishes to encamp troops, Xiao Mi's remaining army is still there;
translations.idiomatic: Just when we would need to encamp, Xiao Mi's remaining forces are still in the field;

sentences.zh: [10]欲言無糧，運船復至。

translations.literal: [10] When one would say there is no grain, transport ships again arrive.
translations.idiomatic: [10] when we claim they lack grain, supply ships arrive.

sentences.zh: 而欲以八十日糧圖城者，臣未之前聞。

translations.literal: Yet to intend to take a city with eighty days' grain—your subject has never before heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: To besiege a city on eighty days' rations—I have never heard of such a thing.

sentences.zh: 且廣陵、任城可為前戒，豈容今者復欲同之。

translations.literal: Moreover Guangling and Rencheng can serve as prior warnings—how can it be allowed that now again one wishes to do the same?
translations.idiomatic: Guangling and Rencheng should serve as warning enough. How can we repeat the same mistake?

sentences.zh: 今若往也，彼牢城自守，不與人戰，城壍水深，非可填塞，空坐至春，則士自弊苦。

translations.literal: If we go now, they will hold the fortress and not fight; the moat is deep with water—not fillable; sitting idle until spring, then the soldiers will weaken themselves in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: If we go, they will shut themselves in fortress walls and refuse battle. Deep moats cannot be filled. We would sit idle until spring while our men sicken and weary.

sentences.zh: 遣臣赴彼，糧何以致？

translations.literal: Sending your subject there—how would grain be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: If I am sent there, how will grain reach us?

sentences.zh: 夏來之兵，不齎冬服，脫遇冰雪，取濟何方？

translations.literal: Soldiers come in summer, not carrying winter clothing—if we encounter ice and snow, where to seek relief?
translations.idiomatic: Summer troops carry no winter gear. If we meet ice and snow, where shall we find relief?

sentences.zh: 臣寧荷怯懦不進之責，不受敗損空行之罪。

translations.literal: Your subject would rather bear the blame of cowardice in not advancing, than accept the crime of defeat, loss, and empty marching.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather accept blame for cowardice than bear guilt for a doomed march ending in defeat.

sentences.zh: 鍾離天險，朝貴所具，若有內應，則所不知，如其無也，必無克狀。

translations.literal: Zhongli is heaven's peril—the court nobles know this in detail; if there is internal collusion, that I do not know; if there is none, assuredly there is no prospect of capture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli is a natural fortress—the court officials know this well. If there is inside help, I cannot say; without it, capture is impossible.

sentences.zh: 若其不復，其辱如何！

translations.literal: If it is not recovered, what shame!
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to take it, the disgrace will be unbearable!

sentences.zh: 若信臣言也，願賜臣停；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty trusts your subject's words, I pray grant your subject halt;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty credits my words, I beg permission to halt.

sentences.zh: 若謂臣難行求回，臣所領兵統悉付中山，任其處分，臣求單騎隨逐東西。

translations.literal: If you say your subject finds it hard and seeks return, all military commands your subject leads I entirely entrust to Zhongshan, let him dispose as he will; your subject requests to follow east and west alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: If you deem me unwilling and seeking retreat, I will transfer all my troops to Prince Zhongshan for his disposition. I ask only to follow the campaign on horseback alone.

sentences.zh: 且俗諺云，耕則問田奴，絹則問織婢。

translations.literal: Moreover a common proverb says: for plowing ask the field slave; for silk ask the weaving maid.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says: ask the field hand about plowing, the weaver about silk.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不武，忝備征將，前宜可否，頗實知之，臣既謂難，何容強遣。

translations.literal: Your subject though not martial, shamefully holds the post of campaign general; whether earlier plans were feasible or not, I rather truly know; since your subject already says it is difficult, how can I be forcibly dispatched?
translations.idiomatic: I am no warrior, yet I am a campaign general and know what is feasible. Having said this is impossible, how can I be forced to go?

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「安東頻請罷軍，遲回未往，阻異戎規，殊乖至望。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "Eastern Pacifier repeatedly requests to halt the army, delays and has not gone, obstructing and differing from the military plan—greatly contrary to utmost hope.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "The General Who Pacifies the East repeatedly asks to stand down, dallies without advancing, and obstructs the military plan—far from what we expect.

sentences.zh: 士馬既殷，無容停積，宜務神速，東西齊契，乘勝掃殄，以赴機會。

translations.literal: Soldiers and horses being abundant, there is no room to halt and accumulate; you should strive for swift spirit, east and west in mutual accord, riding victory to sweep and exterminate, to meet the opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: Our forces are ready and must not lie idle. Move swiftly, coordinate east and west, ride the victory to annihilate the enemy, and seize the moment."

sentences.zh: 」巒累表求還，世宗許之。

translations.literal: " Luan repeatedly memorialized requesting return; Emperor Xuanwu permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Luan petitioned repeatedly to withdraw, and Emperor Xuanwu consented.

sentences.zh: 英果敗退，時人伏其識略。

translations.literal: Ying indeed was defeated and retreated; men of the time admired his foresight and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying was indeed defeated and driven back, and contemporaries admired Luan's foresight.

sentences.zh: 初，侍中盧昶與巒不平，昶與元暉俱世宗所寵，御史中尉崔亮，昶之黨也。

translations.literal: At first, Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang was on bad terms with Luan. Chang and Yuan Hui were both favorites of Emperor Xuanwu. Cui Liang, Imperial Censor-in-Chief, was of Chang's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang and Luan were at odds. Both Chang and Yuan Hui enjoyed Emperor Xuanwu's favor, and Imperial Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang belonged to Chang's faction.

sentences.zh: 昶、暉令亮糾巒，事成許言於世宗以亮為侍中。

translations.literal: Chang and Hui had Liang investigate Luan, promising that if the affair succeeded they would speak to Emperor Xuanwu to appoint Liang as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and Hui set Liang on Luan's trail, promising that if the case succeeded they would recommend Liang to Emperor Xuanwu for appointment as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 亮於是奏劾巒在漢中掠良人為奴婢。

translations.literal: Liang thereupon memorialized impeaching Luan for seizing upright people in Hanzhong and making them slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then memorialized the throne, accusing Luan of seizing innocent people in Hanzhong and reducing them to bondage.

sentences.zh: 巒懼為昶等所陷，乃以漢中所得巴西太守龐景民女化生等二十餘口與暉。

translations.literal: Luan, fearing he would be trapped by Chang and the others, therefore gave to Hui more than twenty persons he had obtained in Hanzhong, including Huasheng, daughter of Pang Jingmin, Governor of Baxi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing entrapment by Chang and his allies, Luan sent Hui more than twenty captives taken in Hanzhong, among them Huasheng, daughter of Pang Jingmin, governor of Baxi.

sentences.zh: 化生等數人，奇色也，暉大悅，乃背昶為巒言於世宗云：「巒新有大功，已經赦宥，不宜方為此獄也。

translations.literal: Huasheng and several others were of extraordinary beauty. Hui was greatly pleased and, turning against Chang, spoke for Luan to Emperor Xuanwu, saying: "Luan has newly achieved great merit and has already been pardoned. It is not fitting to raise this case just now.
translations.idiomatic: Huasheng and several of the women were of rare beauty. Hui was delighted, broke with Chang, and pleaded Luan's cause before Emperor Xuanwu: "Luan has just won a great victory and already received pardon. It is unseemly to reopen this prosecution now.

sentences.zh: 」世宗納之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanwu accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu agreed.

sentences.zh: 高肇以巒有克敵之效，而為昶等所排，助巒申釋，故得不坐。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, because Luan had the effect of defeating the enemy yet was pushed aside by Chang and the others, helped Luan explain and gain release, so he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, seeing that Luan had defeated the enemy yet was being squeezed out by Chang's faction, helped clear him, and so Luan escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 豫州城民白早生殺刺史司馬悅，以城南入，蕭衍遣其冠軍將軍齊苟仁率眾入據懸瓠。

translations.literal: A man of Yuzhou city, Bai Zaosheng, killed Governor Sima Yue, surrendered the south of the city, and Xiao Yan sent his Champion General Qi Gouren to lead troops in and occupy Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zaosheng, a townsman of Yuzhou, killed Governor Sima Yue and opened the southern quarter of the city. Xiao Yan sent his Champion General Qi Gouren to lead troops in and seize Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 詔巒持節率羽林精騎以討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Luan, bearing the staff of authority, to lead elite Feathered Forest cavalry to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Luan Bearer of the Staff and ordered him to lead elite Feathered Forest cavalry against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 封平舒縣開國伯，食邑五百戶，賞宿豫之功也。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ping Shu county with a founding fief, five hundred households for sustenance—a reward for his merit at Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Founding Marquis of Pingshu with a fief of five hundred households, a reward for his victory at Suyu.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨東堂，勞遣巒曰：「司馬悅不慎重門之戒，智不足以謀身，匪直喪元隸豎，[11]乃大虧王略。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu came to the Eastern Hall and saw Luan off with encouragement, saying: "Sima Yue did not heed the warning at the gate of his house; his wisdom was insufficient to preserve himself—not only did he lose his life to a menial, [11] but greatly impaired the royal strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu received Luan at the Eastern Hall and sent him forth with these words: "Sima Yue ignored every warning at his own gate. He lacked the wit to save himself—not only did he lose his head to a lackey, [11] he dealt a grave blow to our royal strategy.

sentences.zh: 懸瓠密邇近畿，東南藩捍，度公之在彼，[12]憂慮尤深。

translations.literal: Xuanhu lies close to the capital region and guards the southeast frontier. Reflecting that you will be there, [12] my worry is especially deep.
