translations.idiomatic: Xuanhu presses close upon the capital and shields the southeast frontier. Knowing you will be there, [12] my anxiety runs especially deep.

sentences.zh: 早生理不獨立，必遠引吳楚，士民同惡，勢或交兵。

translations.literal: Zaosheng by nature cannot stand alone; he is sure to seek distant aid from Wu and Chu. Officials and people share the same hatred—the situation may become an exchange of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Zaosheng cannot stand on his own; he is sure to call in aid from Wu and Chu. Officials and commoners alike hate him, and the fighting may spread.

sentences.zh: 卿文昭武烈，朝之南仲，故令卿星言電邁，出其不意。

translations.literal: You combine civil brilliance with martial prowess—you are the dynasty's Nan Zhong. Therefore I order you to move like star-speech and lightning-speed, catching them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: You unite civil brilliance with martial valor—the court's own pillar of the south. Go swift as starlight and lightning, and take them unawares.

sentences.zh: 卿言早生走也守也？

translations.literal: Tell me—will Zaosheng flee or hold?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me: will Zaosheng flee or stand his ground?

sentences.zh: 何時可以平之？

translations.literal: When can it be pacified?
translations.idiomatic: How soon can the rebellion be crushed?

sentences.zh: 」巒對曰：「早生非有深謀大智能構成此也，但因司馬悅虐於百姓，乘眾怒而為之，民為凶威所懾，不得已而苟附。

translations.literal: " Luan replied: "Zaosheng has no deep stratagem or great wisdom to construct this affair. He only acted because Sima Yue was cruel to the common people, seizing on the people's anger. The people, intimidated by his fierce authority, had no choice but to attach themselves for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: " Luan answered: "Zaosheng has neither deep design nor great talent to have built this rebellion. He merely rode the people's fury after Sima Yue's cruelty. The common folk, cowed by his violence, joined him because they had no choice.

sentences.zh: 假蕭衍軍入應，水路不通，糧運不繼，亦成擒耳，不能為害也。

translations.literal: Even if Xiao Yan's army entered in response—the waterways blocked, grain transport cut off—they too would be captured and could do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Xiao Yan's troops came to his aid, with the waterways blocked and supplies cut off they would be taken too and could do no lasting harm.

sentences.zh: 早生得衍軍之接，溺於利欲之情，必守而不走。

translations.literal: Zaosheng, having received contact with Yan's army, drowning in desire for profit, is sure to hold and not flee.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zaosheng has Liang reinforcements in hand, greed will hold him fast—he will defend the city and not run.

sentences.zh: 今王師若臨，士民必翻然歸順。

translations.literal: Now if the royal army arrives, officials and people will surely turn about and submit.
translations.idiomatic: When our armies arrive, officials and people alike will turn back to us at once.

sentences.zh: 圍之窮城，奔走路絕，不度此年，必傳首京師。

translations.literal: Surround the beleaguered city, cut off escape routes—before this year passes, his head will surely be sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pen him in his exhausted city, cut off every escape, and before the year is out his head will reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 願陛下不足垂慮。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty need not spare a thought of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need give the matter no further thought.

sentences.zh: 」世宗笑曰：「卿言何其壯哉！

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanwu smiled and said: "How bold your words!
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu smiled. "What bold words!

sentences.zh: 深會朕遣卿之意。

translations.literal: You deeply grasp my intention in sending you.
translations.idiomatic: You understand exactly why I am sending you.

sentences.zh: 知卿親老，頻勞於外，然忠孝不俱，才宜救世，不得辭也。」

translations.literal: I know your parents are old and you are repeatedly toiling abroad, yet loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled—the talented should save the age. You may not decline."
translations.idiomatic: I know your parents are aged and that you are worn from repeated campaigns abroad, yet loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fully served, and talent such as yours is meant to save the age. You may not refuse."

sentences.zh: 於是巒率騎八百，倍道兼行，五日次於鮑口。

translations.literal: Thereupon Luan led eight hundred cavalry, traveling double stages and double marches; on the fifth day he halted at Baokou.
translations.idiomatic: Luan then led eight hundred horsemen at forced march, halting at Baokou on the fifth day.

sentences.zh: 賊遣大將軍胡孝智率眾七千，去城二百，逆來拒戰。

translations.literal: The rebels sent Grand General Hu Xiaozhi to lead seven thousand men two hundred li from the city to meet and resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dispatched Grand General Hu Xiaozhi with seven thousand men to meet him two hundred li from the city.

sentences.zh: 巒擊破孝智，乘勝長驅，至於懸瓠。

translations.literal: Luan defeated Xiaozhi, pressed the victory in a long drive, and reached Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Luan routed Xiaozhi, pressed the pursuit, and drove straight to Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 賊出城逆戰，又大破之，因即渡汝。

translations.literal: The rebels came out of the city to meet in battle; he again routed them greatly and immediately crossed the Ru River.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels sallied out to fight, he broke them again and at once crossed the Ru.

sentences.zh: 既而大兵繼至，遂長圍之。

translations.literal: Soon the main army followed and he established a long siege.
translations.idiomatic: The main force soon arrived, and he laid a tight siege.

sentences.zh: 詔加巒使持節、假鎮南將軍、都督南討諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict added to Luan: Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Acting General Who Pacifies the South, Supervisor of All Southern Campaign Forces.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Luan to Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the South, and Commander of All Southern Expeditionary Forces.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍、中山王英南討三關，亦次於懸瓠，以後軍未至，前寇稍多，憚不敢進，乃與巒分兵掎角攻之。

translations.literal: General Who Campaigns South, Prince of Zhongshan Ying, campaigning south against the Three Passes, also halted at Xuanhu. Because the rear army had not arrived and enemy in front were somewhat numerous, he feared and dared not advance, and therefore divided forces with Luan in pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying of Zhongshan, General Who Campaigns South, was also campaigning south against the Three Passes and halted at Xuanhu. His rear guard had not yet come up and the enemy ahead were growing numerous; afraid to advance, he joined Luan in a pincer assault.

sentences.zh: 衍將齊苟仁等二十一人開門出降，即斬早生等同惡數十人。

translations.literal: Yan's generals Qi Gouren and twenty-one others opened the gate and surrendered. He immediately beheaded Zaosheng and several dozen fellow evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Gouren and twenty-one other Liang officers opened the gates and surrendered. Luan at once executed Zaosheng and several dozen of his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 豫州平，巒振旅還京師。

translations.literal: Yuzhou was pacified. Luan reorganized his troops and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuzhou pacified, Luan led his troops home in good order to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨東堂勞之，曰：「卿役不踰時，克清妖醜，鴻勳碩美，可謂無愧古人。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu came to the Eastern Hall to reward him, saying: "Your campaign did not exceed its season; you conquered and cleared the demonic uglies. Grand merit, splendid and fine—you may be said to be unashamed before the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu received him at the Eastern Hall and praised him: "You finished the campaign without delay, crushed the rebel rabble, and won merit grand enough to face the ancients without shame.

sentences.zh: 」巒對曰：「此自陛下聖略威靈，英等將士之力，臣何功之有。

translations.literal: " Luan replied: "This is entirely due to Your Majesty's sagely strategy and august spirit, and the strength of Ying and the other officers and soldiers. What merit has your subject?
translations.idiomatic: " Luan replied, "This was Your Majesty's sage strategy and imperial majesty, and the work of Prince Ying and his officers and men. What merit is mine?

sentences.zh: 」世宗笑曰：「卿匪直一月三捷，所足稱奇，乃存士伯，欲功成而不處。」

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanwu smiled and said: "You are not merely remarkable for three victories in one month—you cherish the manner of a noble knight, wishing to achieve merit yet not occupy it."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu smiled. "Your three victories in a single month are wonder enough—but you also have the true knight's grace: winning glory yet refusing to claim it."

sentences.zh: 巒自宿豫大捷，及平懸瓠，志行修正，不復以財賄為懷，戎資軍實絲毫無犯。

translations.literal: From the great victory at Suyu through the pacification of Xuanhu, Luan corrected his will and conduct. He no longer harbored bribery in mind and did not infringe in the slightest on military funds or army stores.
translations.idiomatic: After his great victory at Suyu and the pacification of Xuanhu, Luan straightened his conduct. He no longer sought bribes and never touched military funds or supplies.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中尚書，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Secretariat and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Palace Secretariat with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年，暴疾卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanchang he died suddenly of illness, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanchang he died suddenly of illness at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 巒才兼文武，朝野瞻望，上下悼惜之。

translations.literal: Luan combined civil and military talent; court and countryside looked up to him; above and below mourned and regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Luan united civil and military gifts, and court and country alike looked to him. High and low mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 詔賻帛四百匹，朝服一襲，贈車騎大將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict granted four hundred bolts of cloth for funeral expenses, one set of court robes, and posthumously conferred General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted four hundred bolts of burial cloth and one set of court robes, and posthumously made him General of Chariots and Cavalry and governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗欲贈冀州，黃門甄琛以巒前曾劾己，乃云：「瀛州巒之本邦，人情所欲。

translations.literal: Early on, Emperor Xuanwu wished to posthumously confer Ji Prefecture. Huangmen Zhen Chen, because Luan had previously impeached him, said: "Ying Prefecture is Luan's native commandery—what people desire by custom.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Xuanwu had wished to grant Jizhou posthumously. But Huangmen Zhen Chen, whom Luan had once impeached, argued: "Yingzhou is Luan's native commandery—the place custom would choose.

sentences.zh: 」乃從之。

translations.literal: " They therefore followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 及琛為詔，乃云「優贈車騎將軍、瀛州刺史」，議者笑琛淺薄。

translations.literal: When Chen drafted the edict, he wrote only "gracefully confer General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Ying Prefecture"—commentators laughed at Chen's pettiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen drafted the edict, he wrote only "honor him as General of Chariots and Cavalry and governor of Yingzhou," omitting the grand general's title. Observers mocked his pettiness.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文定。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Wending.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Wending.

sentences.zh: 子遜，字子言。

translations.literal: His son Sun, courtesy name Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun, courtesy name Ziyan.

sentences.zh: 貌雖陋短，頗有風氣。

translations.literal: Though his appearance was ugly and short, he had considerable bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and short in appearance, he nevertheless carried himself well.

sentences.zh: 解褐司徒行參軍。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the hempen robe he became Staff Adjutant in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he became a staff adjutant in the chancellor's service.

sentences.zh: 襲爵。

translations.literal: He inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 後遷國子博士、本州中正。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University and Rectifier of his native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made erudite of the Imperial University and rectifier of his native prefecture.

sentences.zh: 因謁靈太后，自陳：「功名之子，久抱沉屈。

translations.literal: On an audience with Empress Dowager Ling, he stated himself: "As the son of a man of merit and fame, I have long harbored suppressed grievance.
translations.idiomatic: On audience with Empress Dowager Ling he declared: "As the son of a man of great merit, I have long languished in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 臣父屢為大將，而臣身無軍功階級，臣父唯為忠臣，不為慈父。

translations.literal: My father repeatedly served as a grand general, yet I personally have no military merit rank. My father was only a loyal minister—not a loving father."
translations.idiomatic: My father served repeatedly as a great general, yet I hold no military rank at all. He was a loyal minister to the throne—but no loving father to me."

sentences.zh: 」靈太后慨然，以遜為長兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager was moved and appointed Sun Concurrent Chief Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: " Moved, Empress Dowager Ling appointed Sun concurrent chief director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為安遠將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Governor of Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and governor of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時北蕃多難，稽留不進，免。

translations.literal: At the time the northern frontier had many troubles; he delayed and did not advance, and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier was then in turmoil; he lingered on the road and never took up his post, and was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，除輔國將軍、通直散騎常侍、東道軍司，討逆賊劉舉於濮陽，不克。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang's reign he was appointed General Who Assists the State, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry, and Eastern Route Army Supervisor, to suppress the rebel Liu Ju at Puyang—but failed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaozhuang's reign he was made General Who Assists the State, Regular Attendant of the Fast Cavalry, and eastern-route army supervisor, and sent to suppress the rebel Liu Ju at Puyang—but failed.

sentences.zh: 還，除散騎常侍，加前將軍。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry with the additional title General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Attendant of the Fast Cavalry with the additional rank of General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，坐受任元顥，除名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an he was punished for accepting appointment under Yuan Hao and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an he was stripped of rank for having accepted office under Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 尋除撫軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Tassel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Tassel.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，轉衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Chudi he was transferred to General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chudi he became General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，以本官領嘗藥典御，加車騎將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign, retaining his post he also headed Imperial Taster and Pharmacy Supervisor, with the additional title General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaojing's reign he kept his existing rank, added General of Chariots and Cavalry, and also served as imperial taster and pharmacy supervisor.

sentences.zh: 久之，除大司農卿，與少卿馬慶哲至相糾訟。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Minister of Grand Agriculture and mutually impeached and sued with Vice Minister Ma Qingzhe.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made Minister of Grand Agriculture and fell into repeated mutual accusations with Vice Minister Ma Qingzhe.

sentences.zh: 遜銳於財利，議者鄙之。

translations.literal: Sun was sharp in pursuit of profit; commentators despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun was keen for profit, and public opinion held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 武定四年卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wuding he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Wuding at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、光祿勳卿、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred his former generalship, Minister of Splendid Happiness, and Governor of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted his former general's rank, the title Minister of Splendid Happiness, and the governorship of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子祖微，開府祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Zuo Wei, Libationer of an opening commandery office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuo Wei served as libationer of an opening commandery staff.

sentences.zh: 父喪未終，謀反，伏法。

translations.literal: Before his father's mourning was complete he plotted rebellion and was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Before his father's mourning period had ended he plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 巒弟儒，瀛州鎮遠府長史、給事中。

translations.literal: Luan's younger brother Ru served as Chief Clerk of Ying Prefecture's Distance-Pacifying Office and Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's younger brother Ru was chief clerk of Yingzhou's Distance-Pacifying Office and a supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 儒弟偉，尚書郎中。

translations.literal: Ru's younger brother Wei served as Gentleman of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's younger brother Wei was a gentleman of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈博陵太守。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously conferred Governor of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made governor of Boling.

sentences.zh: 子昕，在文苑傳。

translations.literal: His son Xin—biography in the Literary Garden.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin is treated in the Literary Garden biography.

sentences.zh: 偉弟季彥。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Jiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger brother Jiyan.

sentences.zh: 季彥弟晏，字幼平。

translations.literal: Jiyan's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Youping.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyan's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Youping.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，博涉經史，善談釋老，雅好文詠。

translations.literal: Handsome in bearing, broadly versed in classics and histories, skilled at discussing Buddhism and Daoism, elegantly fond of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing, widely read in the classics and histories, fluent in Buddhist and Daoist discourse, and devoted to poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 起家太學博士、司徒東閤祭酒。

translations.literal: He began his career as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Libationer of the Chancellor's Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as erudite of the Imperial Academy and libationer of the chancellor's Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，為與廣平王懷遊宴，左遷鄚縣令，未之官。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign, for feasting and revelry with Prince of Guangping Huai, he was demoted to Magistrate of Mo county but never took up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was demoted to magistrate of Mo for carousing with Prince Huai of Guangping, but never took up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 除給事中，遷司空主簿、本州中正、汝南王文學。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor, then transferred to Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, Rectifier of his native prefecture, and Literary Instructor to the Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervising censor, then chief clerk of the Ministry of Works, rectifier of his native prefecture, and literary instructor to the Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 稍遷輔國將軍、司空長史、兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted to General Who Assists the State, Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to General Who Assists the State, chief clerk of the Ministry of Works, and concurrent director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以本將軍出為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: With his existing generalship he was sent out as Governor of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: With his existing rank he was sent out as governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 徵為太中大夫、兼丞相高陽王右長史。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Grand Master of the Palace and Concurrent Right Chief Clerk to Chancellor, Prince of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Grand Master of the Palace and concurrent right chief clerk to the Prince of Gaoyang, chancellor of state.

sentences.zh: 尋以本將軍除滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon, with his existing generalship, he was appointed Governor of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made governor of Cangzhou, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，吏民安之。

translations.literal: His administration was pure and quiet; officials and people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was calm and clean, and officials and people alike lived at ease.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: He died during the Xiaochang era, aged fifty-one at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xiaochang era at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈征北將軍、尚書左僕射、瀛州刺史，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred General Who Campaigns North, Left Vice Director of the Ministry, and Governor of Ying Prefecture. Posthumous title: Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Campaigns North, Left Vice Director of the Ministry, and governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 晏篤於義讓，初為南兗州刺史，例得一子解褐，乃啟其孤弟子子慎，年甫十二，而其子已弱冠矣。

translations.literal: Yan was deeply devoted to righteousness and deference. When he first served as Governor of Southern Yan Province, by precedent one son could leave the hempen robe—yet he petitioned for his orphaned brother's son Zishen, who was only twelve, while his own son was already twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was deeply devoted to duty and self-restraint. When he first became governor of Southern Yanzhou, precedent allowed one son to enter office; yet he petitioned for his orphaned brother's son Zishen, then only twelve, though his own son was already twenty.

sentences.zh: 後為滄州，復啟孤兄子昕為府主簿，而其子並未從官。

translations.literal: Later as governor of Cang Prefecture, he again petitioned for his orphaned elder brother's son Xin as Chief Clerk of his commandery office, while his own sons had never held office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as governor of Cangzhou, he again petitioned for his orphaned elder brother's son Xin as chief clerk of his commandery staff, while his own sons held no office at all.

sentences.zh: 世人以此多之。

translations.literal: The world greatly praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: The world praised him widely for this.

sentences.zh: 子測，武定末，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: His son Ce, late in Wuding, served as Palace Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ce, late in Wuding, was palace groom to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 測弟亢，字子高，頗有文學。

translations.literal: Ce's younger brother Kang, courtesy name Zigao, had considerable literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Ce's younger brother Kang, courtesy name Zigao, was a capable man of letters.

sentences.zh: 釋褐司空行參軍。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the hempen robe he became Staff Adjutant in the Ministry of Works office.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he became a staff adjutant in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 遷廣平王開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Prince of Guangping's opening commandery office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant gentleman on the Prince of Guangping's opening commandery staff.

sentences.zh: 兼通直散騎常侍，使於蕭衍，時年二十八。

translations.literal: Concurrent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry, he was envoy to Xiao Yan, aged twenty-eight at the time.
translations.idiomatic: As concurrent Regular Attendant of the Fast Cavalry he was sent as envoy to Xiao Yan at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 還，除平東將軍，齊文襄王大將軍府屬，又轉中外府屬。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, staff member of Grand General Wenxiang of Qi, then transferred to staff member of the Central and Outer Offices.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made General Who Pacifies the East and served on the staff of Wenxiang, Prince of Qi, as grand general; he was later transferred to the central and outer offices staff.

sentences.zh: 武定七年，坐事死於晉陽，年三十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuding he was executed for an offense at Jinyang, aged thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuding he was executed at Jinyang for an offense, aged thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 巒叔祖祐，字宗祐。

translations.literal: Luan's granduncle You, courtesy name Zongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's granduncle You, courtesy name Zongyou.

sentences.zh: 少有學尚，知名於時。

translations.literal: In youth he had scholarly aspirations and was renowned in his time.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he pursued learning and won renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 徵除著作郎，領樂浪王傅。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Gentleman for Compilation, concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to office, he was made gentleman for compilation and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 後假員外散騎常侍，使於劉彧。

translations.literal: Later appointed Acting Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry, envoy to Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Acting Regular Attendant of the Fast Cavalry and sent as envoy to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 以將命之勤，除建威將軍、平原太守，賜爵城平男。

translations.literal: For diligence in carrying the imperial commission, he was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Governor of Pingyuan, and granted the title Baron of Chengping.
translations.idiomatic: For faithful service on his mission he was made General Who Establishes Might and governor of Pingyuan, and enfeoffed as Baron of Chengping.

sentences.zh: 政清刑肅，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Government was clear, punishments were strict, and the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was honest and his punishments firm, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子產，字神寶。

translations.literal: His son Chan, styled Shenbao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chan, courtesy name Shenbao.

sentences.zh: 好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to learning and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 少時作孤蓬賦，為時所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he composed the "Rhapsody on the Lone Tumbleweed," praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he wrote the "Rhapsody on the Lone Tumbleweed," which won contemporary acclaim.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Recommended as Cultivated Talent, appointed Assistant Editor of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Cultivated Talent, he was appointed Assistant Editor of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 假員外常侍、鄚縣子，使於蕭賾。

translations.literal: Acting Supernumerary Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Viscount of Mo County, sent on mission to Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Granted acting rank as Supernumerary Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and made Viscount of Mo County, he was sent on mission to Xiao Ze of Southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 產仍世將命，時人美之。

translations.literal: Chan for generations carried imperial orders; men of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had borne imperial commissions, and contemporaries admired Chan for continuing the tradition.

sentences.zh: 後遷中書侍郎，俄遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Later promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat; soon transferred to Chief Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and soon afterward to Chief Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十六，朝廷嗟惜焉。

translations.literal: He died, aged forty-six; the court lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-six, to the court's deep regret.

sentences.zh: 贈建威將軍、平州刺史、樂城子，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Establishes Might, Governor of Pingzhou, and Viscount of Lecheng; posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Establishes Might, Governor of Pingzhou, and Viscount of Lecheng, with the posthumous title Ding ("Settled").

sentences.zh: 祐從子虬，字神虎。

translations.literal: You's nephew by younger brother Qiu, styled Shenhu.
translations.idiomatic: You's nephew Qiu, courtesy name Shenhu.

sentences.zh: 少為三禮鄭氏學，明經有文思。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Three Rites in the Zheng school, understood the classics, and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied the Three Rites in Zheng Xuan's tradition; he mastered the classics and possessed literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才上第，為中書議郎、尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Recommended as Cultivated Talent with top rank; made Secretariat Discussion Officer and Palace Attendant of the Ministry Director.
translations.idiomatic: Graduating first in the Cultivated Talent examination, he was appointed Secretariat Discussion Officer and Palace Attendant in the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖因公事與語，問朝覲宴饗之禮，虬以經對，大合上旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, on account of official business, spoke with him, asking about the rites of court audience and banquets; Qiu answered with the classics, greatly matching the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: On official business Emperor Xiaowen spoke with him and asked about the rites of imperial audiences and banquets. Qiu answered from the classics in a manner that pleased the emperor greatly.

sentences.zh: 轉司徒屬、國子博士。

translations.literal: Transferred to staff of the Minister of Education and Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the staff of the Minister of Education and appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，尚書令王肅多用新儀，虬往往折以五經正禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu died, Minister Wang Su often employed new ritual forms; Qiu frequently rebutted with the proper rites of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowen's death, Minister of State Wang Su often introduced new ritual forms, but Qiu repeatedly countered with the orthodox rites of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書右丞，徙左丞，多所糾正，臺閣肅然。

translations.literal: Transferred to Right Vice Director of the Ministry; moved to Left Vice Director; many things corrected—the ministries were orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from Right to Left Vice Director of the Ministry, he corrected many abuses and brought order to the central government.

sentences.zh: 時雁門人有害母者，八座奏轘之而潴其室，宥其二子。

translations.literal: At the time a man of Yanmen killed his mother; the Eight Excellencies memorialized that he be drawn apart by chariot and his house flooded, pardoning his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: When a man of Yanmen murdered his mother, the Eight Excellencies recommended that he be torn apart by chariot and his house inundated, while sparing his two sons.

sentences.zh: 虬駁奏云：「君親無將，將而必誅。

translations.literal: Qiu submitted a rebuttal: "Ruler and parent brook no insubordination; once insubordination appears, execution is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu submitted a rebuttal: "Between ruler and parent there can be no insubordination—and once insubordination appears, death is certain.

sentences.zh: 今謀逆者戮及期親，害親者今不及子，既逆甚梟鏡，禽獸之不若，而使禋祀不絕，遺育永傳，非所以勸忠孝之道，存三綱之義。

translations.literal: Now plotters of rebellion are executed together with close kin, yet one who kills a parent is now not punished to the sons—though the crime exceeds the owl and mirror, worse than beasts, yet sacrificial rites do not cease and offspring continue forever—this is not the way to encourage loyalty and filial piety, or preserve the meaning of the Three Bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Today rebels are punished together with their closest kin, yet a man who kills his parent is not punished through his sons. Though such a crime surpasses even the owl and the mirror—worse than any beast—we would still let his sacrifices continue and his line endure forever. That is no way to encourage loyalty and filial piety or uphold the Three Bonds.

sentences.zh: 若聖教含容，不加孥戮，使父子罪不相及，惡止於其身，不則宜投之四裔，敕所在不聽配匹。

translations.literal: If the sage teaching is indulgent and does not extend punishment to offspring, let father and son not suffer each other's crimes, evil stop at one's own person; otherwise they should be cast to the four borderlands, with orders to the regions not to permit marriage.
translations.idiomatic: If the sage teaching is merciful and does not punish offspring, then let father and son not answer for one another's crimes, and let guilt end with the guilty. Otherwise the offenders should be banished to the four borderlands, with orders that no one in those regions may marry them.

sentences.zh: 盤庚言『無令易種於新邑』，漢法五月食梟羹，皆欲絕其類也。

translations.literal: Pan Geng said, 'Do not let them change their seed in the new city'; Han law required eating owl soup in the fifth month—all intending to cut off their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Geng said, 'Do not let them change their seed in the new city,' and Han law required eating owl soup in the fifth month—both measures meant to cut off a wicked line.

sentences.zh: 」奏入，世宗從之。

translations.literal: " The memorial entered; Emperor Shizong approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Xuanwu agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋除司徒右長史，遷龍驤將軍、光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Right Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education; promoted to Dragon-Cavalry General and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Right Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education, then promoted to Dragon-Cavalry General and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 虬母在鄉遇患，請假歸。

translations.literal: Qiu's mother in the countryside fell ill; he requested leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu's mother fell ill at home in the countryside, he asked for leave to return.

sentences.zh: 值秋水暴長，河梁破絕，虬得一小船而渡，漏而不沒，時人異之。

translations.literal: When autumn waters rose violently, the river bridge was destroyed; Qiu obtained a small boat and crossed—leaking yet not sinking; men of the time marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn floods had burst the river banks and destroyed the bridge. Qiu found a small boat and crossed; though it leaked, it did not sink, and people regarded this as remarkable.

sentences.zh: 母喪，哀毀過禮，為時所稱。

translations.literal: At his mother's death, his grief exceeded the rites; praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his grief exceeded what the rites prescribed, and contemporaries praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 年四十九，卒。

translations.literal: Aged forty-nine, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈征虜將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰威。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Youzhou; posthumous title Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Wei ("Authoritative").

sentences.zh: 虬善與人交，清河崔亮、頓丘李平並與親善。

translations.literal: Qiu was good at friendship; Cui Liang of Qinghe and Li Ping of Dunqiu were both close friends.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was gifted at friendship and was close to Cui Liang of Qinghe and Li Ping of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 所作碑頌雜筆三十餘篇。

translations.literal: Inscriptions, eulogies, and miscellaneous writings—more than thirty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than thirty stele inscriptions, eulogies, and assorted writings.

sentences.zh: 有二子。

translations.literal: He had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons.

sentences.zh: 長子臧，在文苑傳。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zang is treated in the Treatise on Literature and the Garden.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zang is treated in the Treatise on Literature.

sentences.zh: 臧弟子才，武定末，太常卿。

translations.literal: Zang's younger brother's son Cai; at the end of Wuding, Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zang's nephew Cai served as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices at the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 虬從子策，亦有才學。

translations.literal: Qiu's nephew by younger brother Ce also had talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's nephew Ce was also a man of talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 卒於齊王儀同開府主簿。

translations.literal: Died as Chief Clerk of the General-in-Chief's Office with Equivalency to the Three Excellencies under the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Chief Clerk of the Prince of Qi's General-in-Chief headquarters.

sentences.zh: 李平，字曇定，頓丘人也，彭城王嶷之長子。

translations.literal: Li Ping, styled Tanding, was a native of Dunqiu, eldest son of Prince Pengcheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping, courtesy name Tanding, came from Dunqiu. He was the eldest son of Prince Pengcheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 少有大度。

translations.literal: In youth he had great magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he was broad-minded and generous.

sentences.zh: 及長，涉獵羣書，好禮、易，頗有文才。

translations.literal: When grown, he ranged through many books, loved the Rites and the Changes, and had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he read widely, loved the Rites and the Book of Changes, and showed considerable literary talent.

sentences.zh: 太和初，拜通直散騎侍郎，高祖禮之甚重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of Direct Communication; Emperor Gaozu treated him with great esteem.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taihe era he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of Direct Communication, and Emperor Xiaowen held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 頻經大憂，居喪以孝稱。

translations.literal: Repeatedly endured great bereavement; in mourning was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Having endured repeated bereavements, he was renowned for filial devotion in mourning.

sentences.zh: 後以例降，襲爵彭城公。

translations.literal: Later by precedent demoted; inherited the title Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following the usual reduction in rank, he inherited the title Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 拜太子中舍人，遷散騎侍郎，舍人如故，遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent; promoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Attendant as before; promoted to Chief Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary while retaining his attendant post, and later to Chief Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 平因侍從容請自效一郡，高祖曰：「卿復欲以吏事自試也。

translations.literal: Ping, while attending, calmly requested to prove himself in one commandery; Emperor Gaozu said: "You again wish to test yourself in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While attending the emperor, Li Ping calmly asked to prove himself in a single commandery. Emperor Xiaowen said, "So you wish to test yourself in administrative affairs again.

sentences.zh: 」拜長樂太守，政務清靜，吏民懷之。

translations.literal: " Appointed Administrator of Changle; administration was clear and quiet; officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Administrator of Changle. His administration was honest and tranquil, and officials and commoners alike held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，以平兼冀州儀同開府長史，甚著聲稱，仍除正長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Ping was additionally made Chief of Staff to the General-in-Chief's Office with Equivalency to the Three Excellencies of Jizhou; his reputation was great; soon made regular Chief of Staff, Administrator as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern campaign, Li Ping was additionally appointed Chief of Staff to the Jizhou General-in-Chief headquarters, where he won great renown. He was soon made regular chief of staff while continuing as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遂行河南尹，豪右權貴憚之。

translations.literal: Before long, he then acted as Director of Henan; powerful gentry and the privileged feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed acting Director of Henan, where powerful families and grasping officials feared him.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，除黃門郎，遷司徒左長史，行尹如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; promoted to Left Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education, acting Director as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Li Ping was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and promoted to Left Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education while continuing as acting Director of Henan.

sentences.zh: 尋以稱職正尹，長史如故。

translations.literal: Soon because of competence made regular Director; Chief of Staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, recognized for his competence, he was made regular Director of Henan while continuing as Chief of Staff.

sentences.zh: 車駕將幸鄴，平上表諫曰：「伏見己丑詔書，雲軒鑾輅，行幸有期，鳳服龍驂，剋駕近日。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was about to visit Ye; Ping submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have seen the edict of the jichou day: cloud-canopied carriage and imperial palanquin, the visit has a set date; phoenix-robed and dragon-harnessed steeds, the journey will mount within recent days.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to visit Ye, Li Ping submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have read the edict of the jichou day: the cloud-canopied carriage and imperial palanquin are to set out on a fixed date; phoenix-robed attendants and dragon-harnessed steeds will depart within days.

sentences.zh: 將欲講武淇陽，大習鄴魏，馳驌騻於綠竹之區，騁驎驥於漳滏之壤。

translations.literal: About to review arms at Qiyang, greatly drill at Ye and Wei, gallop fine steeds in the district of green bamboo, race thoroughbreds on the lands of the Zhang and Fu rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty intends to review troops at Qiyang and hold great exercises in Ye and Wei—to gallop fine horses through the groves of green bamboo and race thoroughbreds across the banks of the Zhang and Fu.

sentences.zh: 斯誠幽顯同忻，人靈共悅。

translations.literal: This truly makes the hidden and manifest alike rejoice, humans and spirits together pleased.
translations.idiomatic: This would indeed bring joy to spirits and men alike.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚管，竊有惑焉。

translations.literal: This subject's foolish narrow view secretly has doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my limited understanding I cannot help but harbor doubts.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 嵩京創構，洛邑俶營，雖年跨十稔，根基未就。

translations.literal: Song capital newly built, Luoyang city just begun—though years span more than ten, foundations are not complete.
translations.idiomatic: The new capital at Songshan and the city of Luoyang have both been under construction for more than ten years, yet their foundations are still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 代民至洛，始欲向盡，資產罄於遷移，牛畜斃於輦運，陵太行之險，越長津之難，辛勤備經，得達京闕，富者猶損太半，貧者可以意知。

translations.literal: People of Dai reaching Luoyang had just exhausted their means; assets spent in relocation, oxen and livestock dead in cart transport; surmounting the peril of Taihang, crossing the hardship of long fords; toil fully endured before reaching the capital gates—the wealthy still lost more than half; the poor one can imagine.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Dai who came to Luoyang had scarcely arrived before their resources were exhausted. Their goods were spent in the move, their oxen and livestock died on the road, and after braving the peril of Taihang and the long river crossings they reached the capital only after every hardship. Even the wealthy lost more than half their property; the poor fared far worse.

sentences.zh: 兼歷歲從戎，不遑啟處，自景明已來，差得休息。

translations.literal: Moreover years spent in the army, no leisure to settle; since Jingming, barely rested.
translations.idiomatic: For years they have served in the army without respite. Only since the Jingming era have they had any real rest.

sentences.zh: 事農者未積二年之儲，築室者裁有數間之屋，莫不肆力伊瀍，人急其務。

translations.literal: Those farming had not accumulated two years' stores; those building houses had scarcely a few rooms—all exerting strength on the Yi and Chan rivers, each urgently at his tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers have not yet stored two years' grain; those building houses have scarcely a few rooms to their name. All are laboring along the Yi and Chan rivers, each pressed by urgent tasks.

sentences.zh: 實宜安靜新人，勸其稼穡，令國有九年之糧，家有水旱之備。

translations.literal: Truly one should quiet the newcomers, encourage their farming, make the state have nine years' grain, households have reserves against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: Surely it is time to let these newcomers settle, encourage their farming, and build up nine years' grain for the state and reserves against flood and drought for every household.

sentences.zh: 若乘之以羈紲，則所廢多矣。

translations.literal: If harnessed with reins and halter, much would be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If they are yoked to corvée and service again, much will be lost.

sentences.zh: 一夫從役，舉家失業。

translations.literal: One man on corvée, the whole household loses livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: When one man is called to service, the whole household loses its livelihood.

sentences.zh: 今復秋稼盈田，禾菽遍野，鑾駕所幸，騰踐必殷。

translations.literal: Now again autumn crops fill the fields, millet and beans cover the wilds—where the imperial palanquin favors, trampling must be heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn crops now fill the fields and grain covers the countryside. Wherever the imperial procession passes, the trampling will be severe.

sentences.zh: 未若端拱中天，坐招四海，耀武崧原，禮射伊洛，士馬無跋涉之勞，兆民有康哉之詠，可不美歟？

translations.literal: Better to sit upright at the center, seated summoning the four seas, display martial glory on the Song plain, perform archery rites at Yi and Luo—soldiers and horses without toil of marching, the myriad people with songs of repose—how could this not be beautiful?
translations.idiomatic: Would it not be better to sit in dignity at the center of the realm and summon the four seas, display martial glory on the Song plain, and perform the archery rites at Yi and Luo—so that soldiers and horses need not weary themselves with long marches and the people may sing of peace? What could be more fitting?

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " Not followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 詔以本官行相州事。

translations.literal: Edict: with his present office, administer Xiangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him to administer Xiangzhou affairs in his current rank.

sentences.zh: 世宗至鄴，親幸平第，見其諸子。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong arrived at Ye; personally visited Ping's residence and saw his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu reached Ye, he personally visited Li Ping's home and met his sons.

sentences.zh: 尋正刺史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Soon made regular Governor; additionally granted General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regular governor and additionally granted the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 平勸課農桑，修飾太學，簡試通儒以充博士，選五郡聰敏者以教之，圖孔子及七十二子於堂，親為立讚。

translations.literal: Ping urged farming and sericulture, renovated the Imperial University, selected and tested accomplished scholars to fill the erudite posts, chose clever youths from five commanderies to teach, painted Confucius and the seventy-two disciples in the hall, personally composing encomia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping promoted agriculture and sericulture, restored the Imperial University, selected accomplished Confucian scholars as erudites, recruited clever students from five commanderies to study under them, and had Confucius and the seventy-two disciples painted in the hall, composing encomia for each himself.

sentences.zh: 前來臺使頗好侵取，平乃畫「履虎尾」、「踐薄冰」於客館，注頌其下，以示誡焉。

translations.literal: Incoming capital envoys greatly loved to seize and take; Ping painted "Treading a tiger's tail" and "Walking on thin ice" in the guest lodge, with encomia appended below to serve as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from the capital were prone to extortion, so Li Ping had "Treading a Tiger's Tail" and "Walking on Thin Ice" painted in the guest lodge with explanatory verses beneath—a pointed warning.

sentences.zh: 加平東將軍，徵拜長兼度支尚書，尋正尚書，領御史中尉。

translations.literal: Added General Who Pacifies the East; summoned and appointed concurrently and as regular Director of the Ministry of Revenue; soon regular Director, also Inspector-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made General Who Pacifies the East, then summoned to serve concurrently and as regular Director of the Ministry of Revenue; soon made regular director while also holding the post of Inspector-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史、京兆王愉反於信都，以平為使持節、都督北討諸軍事、鎮北將軍，行冀州事以討之。

translations.literal: Jizhou Governor, Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled at Xindu; Ping was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Northern Campaign Affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, administering Jizhou affairs to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jizhou Governor and Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled at Xindu, Li Ping was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Northern Expeditionary Forces, and General Who Pacifies the North, with authority over Jizhou affairs to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨式乾殿，勞遣平曰：「愉，朕之元弟，居不疑之地，豺狼之心，不意而發，欲上傾社稷，下殘萬姓。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong at the Shiqian Hall saw Ping off with encouragement, saying: "Yu is my eldest younger brother, in a position beyond suspicion; a wolf's heart, unexpectedly erupting, wishing above to overturn the altars of state, below to slaughter the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: At the Shiqian Hall, Emperor Xuanwu bid Li Ping farewell with these words: "Yu is my own brother, placed in a position beyond suspicion. Yet a wolf's heart has burst forth unlooked-for: he would overturn the altars of state above and slaughter the people below.

sentences.zh: 大義滅親，夫豈獲止。

translations.literal: Great righteousness destroys kin—how could one stop short?
translations.idiomatic: When great righteousness demands the destruction of kin, who may hold back?

sentences.zh: 周公行之於古，朕亦當行之於今。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou did this in antiquity; I too must do it today.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou did this in antiquity; I must do the same today.

sentences.zh: 委卿以專征之任，必令應期摧殄，務盡經略之規，勿虧推轂之寄也。

translations.literal: I entrust you with sole campaign authority; you must make sure to destroy him on schedule, fully exhaust the plans of strategy, and do not fail the trust placed in you as commander.
translations.idiomatic: I entrust you with sole command. You must destroy him at the appointed time, carry out every measure of strategy, and not betray the trust I place in you as my chosen commander.

sentences.zh: 何圖今日言及斯事。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that today I must speak of such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought I would ever have to speak of such a thing.

sentences.zh: 」因歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 平對曰：「臣愉天迷其心，構此梟悖。

translations.literal: Ping replied: "Your subject—Yu heaven has maddened his heart, constructing this rebellious wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping replied, "Yu has lost his mind to heaven and raised this wicked rebellion.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以臣不武，委以總督之任，今大宥既敷，便應有征無戰。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, not deeming your subject unwarlike, has entrusted him with overall command; now that the great pardon has been proclaimed, there should be campaign without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, not deeming me unfit for war, has entrusted me with overall command. Now that the great pardon has been proclaimed, the campaign should require no fighting.

sentences.zh: 脫守迷不悟者，當仰憑天威，抑厲將士，譬猶太陽之消微露，巨海之蕩熒燭，天時人事，滅在昭然。

translations.literal: If any stubbornly hold out in delusion, I shall rely on Heaven's majesty, rouse and steel the officers and soldiers—like the sun dispelling morning dew, like the great sea washing away a flickering candle; Heaven's season and human affairs make destruction manifest.
translations.idiomatic: If any hold out in stubborn delusion, I shall rely on Heaven's majesty and steel the troops—as the sun dispels morning dew, as the great sea washes away a flickering candle. Heaven and human affairs alike make their destruction plain.

sentences.zh: 如其稽顙軍門，則送之大理，若不悛待戮，則鳴鼓釁鍾，非陛下之事。」

translations.literal: If they bow their foreheads at the army gate, I shall send them to the Court of Justice; if they do not repent and await execution, then drums will sound and bells be struck for battle—that will not be Your Majesty's affair."
translations.idiomatic: If they prostrate themselves at the army gate, I shall send them to the Court of Justice. If they refuse to repent and await execution, then drums will sound and bells be struck—that will be no affair of Your Majesty's."

sentences.zh: 平進次經縣，諸軍大集。

translations.literal: Ping advanced and halted at Jing County; the armies gathered in force.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping advanced and encamped at Jing County, where the armies assembled in force.

sentences.zh: 夜有蠻兵數千斫平前壘，矢及平帳，平堅臥不動，俄而乃定。

translations.literal: At night several thousand barbarian soldiers cut at Ping's forward rampart; arrows reached Ping's tent; Ping lay firm and did not move; soon it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: By night several thousand tribal soldiers attacked Li Ping's forward rampart; arrows struck his tent, yet he lay still and did not stir until the disturbance subsided.

sentences.zh: 遂至冀州城南十六里。

translations.literal: Then reached sixteen li south of Jizhou city.
translations.idiomatic: He then reached a point sixteen li south of Jizhou city.

sentences.zh: 賊攻圍濟州軍，拔柵填塹，未滿者數尺。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked and besieged the Jizhou army, pulled palisades and filled moats—where not yet full, several chi remained.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked and besieged the Jizhou army, tearing up palisades and filling the moat until only a few chi remained unfilled.

sentences.zh: 諸將合戰，無利而還，憚於更進。

translations.literal: The generals joined battle, gained no advantage and withdrew, fearing to advance again.
translations.idiomatic: The generals joined battle but gained no advantage and withdrew, afraid to press forward again.

sentences.zh: 平親入行間，勸以重賞，士卒乃前，大破逆眾。

translations.literal: Ping personally entered the ranks, encouraging with heavy rewards; the soldiers then advanced and greatly broke the rebel host.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping personally entered the ranks and promised heavy rewards. The soldiers then pressed forward and routed the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 愉時墜馬，乃有一人下馬授愉，止而鬬死。

translations.literal: Yu at the time fell from his horse; then one man dismounted and gave Yu his horse, stopping to fight and die.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fell from his horse; a man dismounted, gave Yu his own mount, and fought to the death where he stood.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北，至於城門，斬首數萬級，遂圍城燒門。

translations.literal: Pressing victory in pursuit northward, reaching the city gate, heads cut numbered in the tens of thousands; then besieged the city and burned the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the victory northward to the city gate, they took tens of thousands of heads, then besieged the city and set fire to the gate.

sentences.zh: 愉與百餘騎突門出走，遣統軍叔孫頭追之，去信都十里擒愉。

translations.literal: Yu with a hundred-odd horsemen burst through the gate and fled; dispatched Commander Shusun Tou to pursue; ten li from Xindu captured Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu broke out of the gate with a little over a hundred horsemen. Li Ping sent Commander Shusun Tou in pursuit and captured Yu ten li from Xindu.

sentences.zh: 冀州平，世宗遣兼給事黃門侍郎、祕書丞元梵宣旨慰勞。

translations.literal: Jizhou pacified, Emperor Shizong dispatched Concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate and Secretary Director Yuan Fan to proclaim the imperial message and offer consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When Jizhou was pacified, Emperor Xuanwu dispatched Concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate and Secretary Director Yuan Fan to convey the imperial message and offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 徵還京師，以本官領相州大中正。

translations.literal: Summoned back to the capital; with his present office also made Chief Rectifier of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and, retaining his present office, was also made Chief Rectifier of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 平先為尚書令高肇、侍御史王顯所恨，後顯代平為中尉，平加散騎常侍，顯劾平在冀州隱截官口，肇又扶成其狀，奏除平名。

translations.literal: Ping had earlier been hated by Minister Wang Gao and Attendant Censor Wang Xian; later Xian replaced Ping as Inspector-in-Chief; Ping was added as Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; Xian impeached Ping for in Jizhou concealing and intercepting official laborers; Gao also helped establish the case; memorialized to remove Ping's name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping had long been hated by Minister of State Gao Zhao and Attendant Censor Wang Xian. When Xian replaced Ping as Inspector-in-Chief, Ping was additionally made Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary. Xian then impeached him for concealing and intercepting registered corvée laborers in Jizhou; Gao helped establish the case, and a memorial was submitted stripping Li Ping of his office and rank.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，詔復官爵，除其定冀之勳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yan chang, edict restored office and title, removing his merit for pacifying Ji.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yan chang era, an edict restored his office and title but stripped him of his merit for pacifying Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 前來良賤之訟，多有積年不決，平奏不問真偽，一以景明年前為限，於是諍訟止息。

translations.literal: Previously lawsuits over free and servile status had often gone unresolved for many years; Ping memorialized that truth and falsehood not be inquired into, all limited to before the Jingming year; thereby contentious lawsuits ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Lawsuits over free and servile status had often dragged on unresolved for years. Li Ping memorialized that such cases, without inquiry into truth or falsehood, be limited to those arising before the Jingming era. Contentious litigation then ceased.

sentences.zh: 武川鎮民飢，鎮將任款請貸未許，擅開倉賑恤，有司繩以費散之條，免其官爵。

translations.literal: The people of Wuchuan garrison were hungry; Garrison Commander Ren Kuan requested grain on loan but was not permitted; he on his own opened the granary for relief; the responsible offices bound him under the statute on wasteful dispersal and removed his office and title.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Wuchuan Garrison faced famine, Garrison Commander Ren Kuan requested grain on loan but was refused; he opened the granary on his own authority to relieve them. The responsible offices charged him under the statute on wasteful dispersal of stores and stripped him of office and rank.

sentences.zh: 平奏款意在濟人，心無不善，世宗原之。

translations.literal: Ping memorialized that Kuan's intent was to aid the people, his heart without evil; Emperor Shizong pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping memorialized that Ren Kuan's intent had been to save the people and that his heart held no evil. Emperor Xuanwu pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，尚書如故。

translations.literal: Transferred to Director of the Secretariat; Minister as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat while retaining his ministry post.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，轉吏部尚書，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong, transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, added General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, he was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 平高明強濟，所在有聲，但以性急為累。

translations.literal: Ping was outstanding, bright, strong, and effective; wherever he served he won renown, but his quick temper was his burden.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping was gifted, forceful, and capable; he earned a reputation wherever he served, though his impetuous temperament was his one flaw.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄奏理平定冀之勳，請酬以山河之賞。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Rencheng, Yuan Cheng, memorialized to settle the merit of Ping's pacification of Ji, requesting reward with the bounty of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Yuan Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, submitted a memorial settling the record of Li Ping's pacification of Ji and asking that he be rewarded with a territorial enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 靈太后乃封武邑郡開國公，食邑一千五百戶，縑二千五百匹。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling thereupon enfeoffed him as Duke of Wuyi commandery with state-founding rank, with a fief of one thousand five hundred households and two thousand five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling then created him Duke of Wuyi commandery with state-founding rank, granting a fief of fifteen hundred households and twenty-five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭衍遣其左游擊將軍趙祖悅偷據西硤石，眾至數萬，以逼壽春。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Yan had sent his Left Mobile General Zhao Zu Yue to seize West Xiashi by stealth; his forces reached tens of thousands and pressed upon Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Yan had sent his Left Mobile General Zhao Zu Yue to seize West Xiashi by surprise; his army numbered in the tens of thousands and threatened Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 鎮南崔亮攻之，未克，又與李崇乖貳。

translations.literal: Pacifier of the South Cui Liang attacked him but could not take the place, and he also fell at odds with Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang, Pacifier of the South, besieged him without success, and he also fell out with Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 詔平以本官使持節、鎮軍大將軍、兼尚書右僕射為行臺，節度諸軍，東西州將一以禀之，如有乖異，以軍法從事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ping, with his existing office, as Commissioner Bearing Credentials, General Who Guards the Army, and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, to serve as mobile headquarters, directing all armies; generals of the eastern and western provinces were all to report to him, and any who deviated were to be dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Li Ping, retaining his existing rank, as Commissioner Bearing Credentials, General Who Guards the Army, and concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with authority as mobile headquarters over all armies. Generals of the eastern and western provinces were to take orders from him alone, and any who defied him were to be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 詔平長子奬以通直郎從，賜平縑帛百段、紫納金裝衫甲一領，賜奬縑布六十段、絳衲襖一領。

translations.literal: An edict made Ping's eldest son Jiang a Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary to accompany him; Ping was granted one hundred bolts of silk and brocade and one suit of purple padded armor with gold fittings, and Jiang was granted sixty bolts of silk and hemp and one padded jacket of crimson cloth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Li Ping's eldest son Jiang Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary to accompany him. Li Ping received one hundred bolts of silk and brocade and a suit of purple padded armor with gold fittings; Jiang received sixty bolts of silk and hemp and a padded jacket of crimson cloth.

sentences.zh: 父子重列，拜受家庭，觀者榮之。

translations.literal: Father and son stood in paired ranks, bowing to receive the gifts at home; onlookers took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son stood side by side to bow and receive the imperial gifts at home, to the envy of all who watched.

sentences.zh: 於是率步騎二千以赴壽春。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led two thousand infantry and cavalry to hasten to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He then led two thousand foot and horse to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 平巡視硤石內外，知其盈虛之所。

translations.literal: Ping inspected Xiashi inside and out and learned where its strengths and weaknesses lay.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping surveyed Xiashi inside and out and learned where its strengths and weaknesses lay.

sentences.zh: 嚴勒崇、亮，令水陸兼備，剋期齊舉。

translations.literal: He strictly pressed Chong and Liang, ordering both land and water forces fully prepared to strike together on the appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Li Chong and Cui Liang hard, ordering land and water forces alike made ready to attack together on the fixed day.

sentences.zh: 崇、亮憚之，無敢乖互。

translations.literal: Chong and Liang feared him and dared not defy one another.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong and Cui Liang feared him and no longer dared to work at cross purposes.

sentences.zh: 頻日交戰，屢破賊軍。

translations.literal: Day after day they joined battle and repeatedly broke the rebel army.
translations.idiomatic: Battle followed battle for days on end, and the rebel army was broken again and again.

sentences.zh: 安南將軍崔延伯立橋於下蔡，以拒賊之援軍。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Cui Yanbo built a bridge at Xia Cai to block the rebels' relief army.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanbo, General Who Pacifies the South, built a bridge at Xia Cai to block the rebels' relief force.

sentences.zh: 賊將王神念、昌義之等不得進救，祖悅守死窮城。

translations.literal: The rebel generals Wang Shennian, Chang Yizhi, and others could not advance to the rescue; Zu Yue held the doomed city to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel generals Wang Shennian, Chang Yizhi, and others could not break through to relieve the city; Zu Yue held the hopeless fortress to the last.

sentences.zh: 平乃部分攻之。

translations.literal: Ping then divided his forces and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping then divided his forces and pressed the assault.

sentences.zh: 令崔亮督陸卒攻其城西，李崇勒水軍擊其東面，然後鼓噪，南北俱上。

translations.literal: He ordered Cui Liang to command the land troops in attacking the west of the city and Li Chong to drive the water force against its east; then, at the drum and shout, both north and south went up together.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Cui Liang to lead the infantry against the west wall and Li Chong to drive the fleet against the east; then, at the war cry, both wings surged forward together.

sentences.zh: 賊眾周章，東西赴戰。

translations.literal: The rebel masses were thrown into confusion and rushed to fight east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel host fell into confusion and rushed back and forth between east and west.

sentences.zh: 屠賊外城，賊之將士相率歸附。

translations.literal: They slaughtered their way into the outer city, and the rebel officers and soldiers submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the outer city, and rebel officers and soldiers surrendered in waves.

sentences.zh: 袓悅率其餘眾固保南城，通夜攻守，至明乃降。

translations.literal: Zu Yue led his remaining force to hold fast in the south city; all night they fought attack and defense, and at dawn he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue gathered his remaining men in the south city and fought through the night; at dawn he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 斬袓悅，送首於洛，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Zu Yue was beheaded and his head sent to Luoyang; captives taken were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue was beheaded and his head sent to Luoyang; the prisoners taken were very many.

sentences.zh: 以功遷尚書右僕射，加散騎常侍，將軍如故。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with added rank as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, while retaining his general's commission.

sentences.zh: 平還京師，靈太后見於宣光殿，賜以金裝刀杖一口。

translations.literal: When Ping returned to the capital, Empress Dowager Ling received him in the Hall of Illuminated Glory and granted him one gold-fitted sword and staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ping returned to the capital, Empress Dowager Ling received him in the Hall of Illuminated Glory and granted him a sword and staff with gold fittings.

sentences.zh: 時南徐州表云，蕭衍堰淮水為患，詔公卿議之，平以為不假兵力，終自毀壞。

translations.literal: At that time Southern Xuzhou memorialized that Xiao Yan's dam on the Huai River was causing harm; an edict ordered the high officials to discuss it, and Ping held that without need of military force it would in the end destroy itself.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Xuzhou then reported that Xiao Yan's dam on the Huai was causing damage. The court ordered the high officials to debate the matter, and Li Ping argued that it needed no troops and would collapse of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 及淮堰破，靈太后大悅，引群臣入宴，敕平前鳴簫管，肅宗手賜縑布百段。

translations.literal: When the Huai dam broke, Empress Dowager Ling was greatly pleased; she led the ministers in to feast, ordered Ping forward to play pipes and flutes, and Emperor Xiaozong personally granted him one hundred bolts of silk and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai dam gave way, Empress Dowager Ling was delighted. She brought the ministers in to feast, had Li Ping step forward to play pipes and flutes, and Emperor Xiaozong personally granted him one hundred bolts of silk and hemp.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年冬卒，遺令薄葬。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Xiping he died, leaving instructions for a plain burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of Xiping 1, leaving orders for a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 詔給東園祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲、帛七百匹。

translations.literal: An edict granted the eastern garden secret coffin, one set of court robes, one suit of clothing, and seven hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him the eastern garden secret coffin, one set of court robes, one suit of clothing, and seven hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 靈太后為舉哀於東堂。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling held mourning rites for him in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling held mourning rites for him in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史，諡文烈公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Ji province, with the posthumous epithet Duke Wenlie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Ji province, with the posthumous epithet Duke Wenlie.

sentences.zh: 平自在度支，至於端副，夙夜在公，孜孜匪懈，凡處機密十有餘年，有獻替之稱。

translations.literal: From the time Ping held the Directorate of Revenue to his senior ministerial rank, he rose early and retired late in public service, diligent and never slack; in all he handled confidential affairs for more than ten years and won praise for offering counsel.
translations.idiomatic: From his years as Director of Revenue to his tenure at the apex of government, Li Ping rose early and worked late, tireless in office; for more than ten years he handled state secrets and was praised for counsel that improved policy.

sentences.zh: 所製詩賦箴諫詠頌，[13]別有集錄。

translations.literal: The poems, rhapsodies, admonitions, remonstrances, songs, and eulogies he composed, [13] were separately collected in a compilation.
translations.idiomatic: The poems, rhapsodies, admonitions, remonstrances, songs, and eulogies he composed [13] were gathered in a separate collection.

sentences.zh: 平長子奬，字遵穆，襲。

translations.literal: Ping's eldest son Jiang, styled Zunmu, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping's eldest son Jiang, courtesy name Zunmu, succeeded to his father's rank.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁偉，有當世才度。

translations.literal: His appearance was tall and imposing, and he had the talent and measure of his age.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing in bearing, with the talent and stature to match his times.

sentences.zh: 自太尉參軍事，稍遷通直郎、中書侍郎、直閤將軍、吏部郎中、征虜將軍，遷安東將軍、光祿大夫，仍吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Starting as staff officer to the Grand Commandant, he was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Vice Director of the Secretariat, General of the Direct Gate, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, then General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and again Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning as an aide to the Grand Commandant, he rose step by step through Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Vice Director of the Secretariat, General of the Direct Gate, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and General Who Punishes the Barbarians, then to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and again Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 又以本官兼尚書，出為撫軍將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: With his existing office he was also made Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, then sent out as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Concurrent Director of the Secretariat in his existing rank and sent out as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 初，元叉擅朝，奬為其親待，頻居顯要。

translations.literal: At first, when Yuan Cha monopolized the court, Jiang was treated as a close favorite and repeatedly held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha first dominated the court, Jiang was treated as a close favorite and repeatedly held high office.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，削除官爵。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling resumed power, his offices and titles were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling resumed power, his offices and titles were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，為散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、河南尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 奬前後所歷，皆以明濟著稱。

translations.literal: In every post Jiang had held, before and after, he was known for clarity and effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he had held, Jiang was known for clear and effective governance.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，顥以奬兼尚書右僕射，慰勞徐州羽林及城人，不承顥旨，害奬，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Hao made Jiang Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat to comfort the Xuzhou guard and the people of the city; they refused to obey Hao's orders and killed Jiang, sending his head to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he made Jiang Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat to reassure the Xuzhou guard and the city's people; they refused Hao's orders, killed Jiang, and sent his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，奬故吏通直散騎常侍宋遊道上書理奬曰：「臣聞賞善罰惡，謂之二機，有道存焉，所貴不濫。

translations.literal: In the time of the Deposed Emperor, Jiang's former subordinate Song Youdao, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Direct Gate, submitted a memorial on Jiang's behalf, saying: "Your subject has heard that rewarding good and punishing evil are called the two levers; the Way resides in them, and what is prized is that they not be applied amiss.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Deposed Emperor, Jiang's former subordinate Song Youdao, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Direct Gate, submitted a memorial in his defense, saying: "Your subject has heard that rewarding good and punishing evil are the two levers of rule; the Way rests in them, and what matters is that they never be misapplied.

sentences.zh: 是以子胥無罪，吳人痛之；

translations.literal: Thus when Wu Zixu was innocent, the people of Wu grieved for him;
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zixu was innocent, the people of Wu grieved for him;

sentences.zh: 郤宛不幸，國言未息。

translations.literal: when Xi Wan met misfortune, the state's talk did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: when Xi Wan met with misfortune, the kingdom's lament never ceased.

sentences.zh: 故河南尹李奬，門居戚里，世擅名家，有此良才，是兼周用。

translations.literal: The former Governor of Henan, Li Jiang, stood among the imperial kin, and his house had long been a famous clan; with such fine talent he was fit for every use.
translations.idiomatic: The former Governor of Henan, Li Jiang, belonged to the imperial kin; his family had long been a house of renown, and with such talent he was fit for every task.

sentences.zh: 自少及長，忠孝為心，入朝出牧，清明流譽。

translations.literal: From youth to age, loyalty and filial piety were his heart; entering court or going out to govern a province, he was clear and famed.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to age loyalty and filial piety filled his heart; whether at court or governing a province, he won fame for clarity.

sentences.zh: 襟懷放暢，風神爽發，實廊廟之瑚璉，社稷之楨幹。

translations.literal: His breast was open and free, his spirit bright and quick; he was truly a ritual vessel of the hall and pillar of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Open in spirit and bright in bearing, he was truly a ritual vessel of the court and a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 往歲，北海竊據，負扆當朝，王公卿士，俛眉從事。

translations.literal: In years past, when Beihai seized power and sat at the throne, princes, dukes, ministers, and gentry bowed their brows and served.
translations.idiomatic: In years past, when Beihai seized power and held the throne, princes, dukes, ministers, and officials all bowed and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 而奬闔門百口，同居京洛，既被覊縶，自拔無由。

translations.literal: Yet Jiang's whole household of a hundred mouths lived together in the capital; once bound and held, there was no way to free himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jiang's household of a hundred mouths lived together in the capital; once bound and held captive, he had no way to break free.

sentences.zh: 託使東南，情存避難，當時物論謂其得所。

translations.literal: Entrusted with a mission to the southeast, his heart sought refuge from disaster; opinion at the time held that he had found the right course.
translations.idiomatic: Sent on a mission to the southeast, he sought refuge from disaster; public opinion at the time held that he had chosen wisely.

sentences.zh: 然北海未敗之日，徐州刺史元孚為其純臣，莫之敢距，表啟相望，遲速唯命。

translations.literal: Yet before Beihai's defeat, Xuzhou Governor Yuan Fu was his loyal minister and none dared resist; memorials and reports followed one after another, and quick or slow obeyed his word alone.
