translations.idiomatic: Yet before Beihai's defeat, Xuzhou Governor Yuan Fu was his loyal servant and none dared resist him; memorial after memorial went out, and every move awaited his command.

sentences.zh: 及皇輿返正，神器斯復，輕薄之徒，共生僥倖，詭言要賞，曲道求通，濫及善人，稱為己力。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the rightful order and the sacred vessel was restored, frivolous men together nursed vain hopes; with crooked words they sought reward, by devious paths they sought advancement, wrongly implicating good men and calling it their own achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne was restored and the sacred vessel recovered, frivolous men seized on vain hopes; with twisted words they claimed reward, by crooked paths they sought favor, and they dragged good men into guilt and called it their own merit.

sentences.zh: 若以奬受命賊朝，語跡成罪，便與天下共當此責。

translations.literal: If accepting office under the rebel court makes Jiang guilty by word and deed, then the whole realm must share this blame.
translations.idiomatic: If accepting office under the rebel court makes Jiang guilty by word and deed, then the whole realm must bear that guilt together.

sentences.zh: 于時朝旨唯命免官，亦既經恩，方加酷濫。

translations.literal: At that time the court's intent was only to order dismissal from office; already having received grace, they then added cruel excess.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court's intent was only to dismiss him from office; having already shown mercy, they then added cruel excess.

sentences.zh: 伊昔具臣，比肩賊所，身臨河上，日尋干戈，時逢寬政，任遇不改。

translations.literal: In former times worthy ministers stood shoulder to shoulder in the rebel camp, themselves on the river bank day after day seeking battle; when a lenient policy came, their appointments did not change.
translations.idiomatic: In former times worthy ministers stood side by side in the rebel camp, themselves on the riverbank day after day at war; when leniency prevailed, their appointments were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 一介使人，獨嬰斯戮，凡在有心，孰不嗟悼！

translations.literal: One lone envoy alone suffered this execution; all who have a heart—who does not sigh and mourn!
translations.idiomatic: One lone envoy alone suffered this execution; all who have a heart—who could fail to mourn him!

sentences.zh: 前朝所以論功者，見其邊人且相慰悅，其猶郭默生亂，劉胤懸首，事乃權宜，蓋非實錄。

translations.literal: The reason the previous court counted it merit was that they saw the border people somewhat comforted and pleased; it was like when Guo Mo raised rebellion and Liu Yin's head was hung— the affair was expedient and not truly recorded fact.
translations.idiomatic: The previous court counted it merit only because the border people seemed somewhat reassured; it was like when Guo Mo raised rebellion and Liu Yin's head was displayed—the affair was expedient and hardly a true record.

sentences.zh: 昔鄧艾下世，段灼理其冤；

translations.literal: In the past, when Deng Ai died, Duan Zhuo cleared his wrong;
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Deng Ai died, Duan Zhuo cleared his wrong;

sentences.zh: 馬援物故，朱勃申其屈。

translations.literal: when Ma Yuan passed away, Zhu Bo pleaded his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: when Ma Yuan passed away, Zhu Bo pleaded his grievance.

sentences.zh: 臣雖小人，趣事君子，有懷舊恩，義兼人故，見其若此，久欲陳辭。

translations.literal: Your subject, though a small man, delights in serving gentlemen; cherishing old kindness, his duty also embraces ties of friendship; seeing Jiang treated thus, he has long wished to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, though a humble man, has always wished to serve the worthy; cherishing old kindness and bound by friendship, seeing Jiang treated thus, he has long wished to speak out.

sentences.zh: 含言未吐，遂至今日，幽泉已閉，壟樹成行，內手捫心，顧懷愧慨。

translations.literal: Words held back and not spoken reached today; the dark spring is already closed and tomb trees stand in rows; pressing his hand to his heart within, he looks back with shame and grief.
translations.idiomatic: Words held back have reached this day; the grave is closed and tomb trees stand in rows; pressing hand to heart, he looks back with shame and grief.

sentences.zh: 幸逢興聖，理運唯新，雖曰纂戎，事同創革。

translations.literal: Fortunately one meets a sage in ascent and the order of the age is wholly new; though it is called succeeding to arms, the affair is like founding anew.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately we meet a sage ascending the throne and an age wholly renewed; though called succession, the work is like a new founding.

sentences.zh: 頻有大恩，被於率土，亡官失爵者悉蒙追復。

translations.literal: Great grace has repeatedly been spread over all the land; those who lost office and rank have all received restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Great grace has repeatedly spread over the realm; all who lost office and rank have been restored.

sentences.zh: 而奬雜木猶存，牛車未改。

translations.literal: Yet Jiang, like a worthless tree, still stands, and the ox cart is unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jiang, like a withered stump, still stands unrewarded, and the humble cart of his rank is unchanged.

sentences.zh: 士感知己，懷此無忘，輕率瞽言，干犯輦轂。

translations.literal: A gentleman who knows kindness cannot forget this; with rash blind words he offends the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman who knows kindness cannot forget this; with rash and reckless words he offends the imperial presence.

sentences.zh: 伏願天鑒，賜垂矜覽，加其贈秩，慰此幽魂。

translations.literal: Prostrate, he hopes Heaven's mirror will grant pity and review, adding to his posthumous rank to comfort this shade.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate, he prays that Heaven's mirror may grant pity and review, adding to Jiang's posthumous rank to comfort his shade.

sentences.zh: 」詔贈衞將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: " An edict posthumously honored him as General of the Guard and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict posthumously honored him as General of the Guard and Governor of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 子構，襲。

translations.literal: His son Gou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gou succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 武定末，太子中舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi accepted the abdication, his rank was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 構弟訓，太尉默曹參軍。

translations.literal: Gou's younger brother Xun was a staff officer in the Grand Commandant's Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gou's younger brother Xun was a staff officer in the Grand Commandant's Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奬弟諧，字虔和。

translations.literal: Jiang's younger brother Xie, styled Qianhe.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang's younger brother Xie, courtesy name Qianhe.

sentences.zh: 風流閑潤，博學有文辯，當時才俊，咸相欽賞。

translations.literal: Graceful, refined, and easy in manner, broadly learned with literary eloquence, he was admired by all the talented men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful, refined, and easy in manner, broadly learned and eloquent in writing, he was admired by every talented man of the age.

sentences.zh: 受父前爵彭城侯。

translations.literal: He received his father's former title, Marquis of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's former title, Marquis of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 自太尉參軍，歷尚書郎、徐州北海王顥撫軍府司馬，入為長兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: From staff officer to the Grand Commandant, he passed through Director of the Secretariat, Sima of the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, in Xuzhou, and entered court as Senior Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as an aide to the Grand Commandant, he served as Director of the Secretariat, then as Sima on the Pacification Army staff of Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai, in Xuzhou, and entered court as Senior Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 崔光引為兼著作郎，諧在史職，無所歷意。

translations.literal: Cui Guang brought him in as Concurrent Compiler in the History Office; Xie, in his historiographical post, had no heart for it.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang brought him in as Concurrent Compiler in the History Office, but Xie had no heart for historiography.

sentences.zh: 加輔國將軍、相州大中正、光祿大夫，除金紫光祿大夫，加衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was given added rank as General Who Supports the State, Chief Rectifier of Xiang province, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Purple Seal, with added rank as General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Supports the State, Chief Rectifier of Xiang province, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Purple Seal and General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，除名，乃為述身賦曰：

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, his name was struck from the rolls, and he composed a Rhapsody on Describing My Life, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, his name was struck from the rolls, and he composed a Rhapsody on Describing My Life, saying:

sentences.zh: 夫休咎相躡，禍福相生。

translations.literal: Fortune and misfortune tread on each other's heels; disaster and blessing give birth to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and misfortune tread on each other's heels; disaster and blessing beget one another.

sentences.zh: 龜筮迷其兆，聖達蔽其萌。

translations.literal: Tortoise and milfoil lose their omens; sages and the enlightened hide the first sprout.
translations.idiomatic: Tortoise shells and milfoil stalks fail their omens; even sages cannot see the first sprout.

sentences.zh: 覽成敗於前迹，料趣捨於人情。

translations.literal: Reviewing success and failure in former tracks, gauging advance and retreat by human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Men read success and failure in the tracks of the past and weigh advance and retreat by human feeling.

sentences.zh: 咸爭途以走利，罕外己以逃名。

translations.literal: All contend on the road to chase profit; few turn outward from self to flee fame.
translations.idiomatic: All race the road to profit; few turn outward from self to flee fame.

sentences.zh: 連從車以載禍，多廐馬以取刑。

translations.literal: Linking follow-carts to carry disaster, keeping many stable horses to invite punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They link follow-carts to carry disaster and keep many stable horses to invite punishment.

sentences.zh: 豈知夫一介獨往，乃千乘所不能傾。

translations.literal: How could they know that one man going alone cannot be overturned even by a thousand chariots?
translations.idiomatic: How could they know that one man going alone cannot be overturned even by a thousand chariots?

sentences.zh: 伊薄躬之悔吝，無性命之淑靈。

translations.literal: Alas for my slight person and its regrets; I have no inborn grace of life.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for my slight person and its regrets—I have no inborn grace of life.

sentences.zh: 藉休庸於祖武，仰餘烈於家聲。

translations.literal: I lean on my ancestors' martial merit and look up to the lingering glory of the family name.
translations.idiomatic: I lean on my ancestors' martial merit and look up to the lingering glory of our family name.

sentences.zh: 徒從師以下學，乏遊道於上京。

translations.literal: In vain I followed teachers to learn below; I lacked the way to wander and study in the upper capital.
translations.idiomatic: In vain I followed teachers in humble study; I never found the way to wander and learn in the capital.

sentences.zh: 洎方年之四五，實始筮之弱齡。

translations.literal: When my years reached four or five, it was truly the weak age of first divination.
translations.idiomatic: When my years reached four or five, it was truly the tender age of first divination.

sentences.zh: 爰釋巾而從吏，謬邀寵於時明。

translations.literal: Then I put aside the towel and followed the clerks, wrongly seeking favor in the bright age.
translations.idiomatic: Then I put aside the scholar's towel and followed the clerks, wrongly seeking favor in a bright age.

sentences.zh: 彼□□之赫赫，乃陋周而小漢。

translations.literal: That □□'s splendor made Zhou seem small and Han petty.
translations.idiomatic: That □□'s splendor made Zhou seem small and Han petty.

sentences.zh: 帝文篤其成功，我武治其未亂。

translations.literal: The emperor's culture fixed its achievement; our martial virtue ordered what was not yet in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial culture secured its achievement; our martial virtue ordered what was not yet in disorder.

sentences.zh: 掩四奧而同軌，穆三辰而貞觀。

translations.literal: It covered the four quarters and made one track; it harmonized the three luminaries and kept correct observation.
translations.idiomatic: It covered the four quarters and made one track; it harmonized sun, moon, and stars and kept the realm in right order.

sentences.zh: 威北暢而武戢，鼎南遷而文煥。

translations.literal: Its might flowed north and arms were stilled; the cauldron moved south and culture blazed.
translations.idiomatic: Its might flowed north and arms were stilled; the cauldron moved south and culture blazed.

sentences.zh: 異人相趨於絳闕，鴻生接武於儒館。

translations.literal: Strange men hastened to the crimson gate; great scholars walked in succession at the Confucian halls.
translations.idiomatic: Strange men hastened to the crimson gate; great scholars walked in succession at the halls of learning.

sentences.zh: 總羣雅而同歸，果方員而殊貫。

translations.literal: Gathering all elegance to one return, square and round in fruit yet threaded differently.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering all elegance to one end, square and round in form yet threaded on different strings.

sentences.zh: 伊濫吹之所從，初竊服於宰旅。

translations.literal: From the indiscriminate piping I followed, at first I stole a place among the host of clerks.
translations.idiomatic: From the indiscriminate piping I followed, at first I stole a place among the host of clerks.

sentences.zh: 奉盛王之高義，遊兔園而容與。

translations.literal: Honoring the Prince of Sheng's high righteousness, I wandered the Rabbit Garden at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the Prince of Sheng's high righteousness, I wandered at ease in the Rabbit Garden.

sentences.zh: 綴鴻鷺之末行，連英髦之茂序。

translations.literal: I joined the last rank of wild swans and geese and linked the flourishing order of outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: I joined the last rank of wild swans and geese and linked the flourishing order of outstanding men.

sentences.zh: 及伯舅之西伐，赫靈旗之東舉。

translations.literal: When the emperor's maternal uncle marched west and the blazing imperial banner was raised in the east.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's maternal uncle marched west and the blazing imperial banner was raised in the east.

sentences.zh: 復奉役於前轅，仍執覊於後距。

translations.literal: Again I served in the front axle and still was held in bonds at the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Again I served at the front axle and still was held in bonds at the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 迫玄冬之暮歲，歷關山之遐阻。

translations.literal: Approaching the late years of dark winter, I traversed the distant barriers of the pass mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the deep of dark winter's last days, I crossed the far barriers of the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 風激沙而破石，雪浮河而漫野。

translations.literal: Wind whipped sand and broke stone; snow floated on rivers and spread across the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Wind lashed the sand and shattered stone; snow drifted on the rivers and flooded the plain.

sentences.zh: 樂在志其無端，悲涉物而多緒。

translations.literal: Joy lodged in the heart for no cause; grief touched things and spawned many moods.
translations.idiomatic: Joy rose in the heart without reason; grief touched every thing and bred a tangle of feeling.

sentences.zh: 俄宮車之晏駕，改乘轅而歸予。

translations.literal: Suddenly the imperial carriage halted in death; I changed my carriage shaft and returned to myself.
translations.idiomatic: Then the imperial carriage halted in death, and I changed my axle-shaft and turned homeward.

sentences.zh: 屬推恩之在今，自傍枝而禔福。

translations.literal: It fell in the time of extending grace that I, from a collateral branch, received blessings.
translations.idiomatic: In the season of extended grace, I—a branch of a collateral line—received its blessings.

sentences.zh: 既獻□以命宗，叨微躬於侯服。

translations.literal: Having presented □ to ennoble the ancestral house, I undeservedly received my slight person in marquisate rank.
translations.idiomatic: Having presented □ to ennoble the ancestral house, I undeservedly received a minor place among the enfeoffed lords.

sentences.zh: 禮空文於覜饗，賦無征於湯沐。

translations.literal: Ceremonial visits were empty forms at inspection audiences; feudal dues had no collection for bath grants.
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences were empty ceremony at inspection feasts; feudal dues brought no revenue even for bath grants.

sentences.zh: 思守位而匪懈，每屏居而自肅。

translations.literal: I thought to keep my place without slackening; each time I withdrew to seclusion and kept myself in order.
translations.idiomatic: I resolved to hold my post without slackening, and each time I withdrew to seclusion and kept myself in check.

sentences.zh: 忽忝命於建禮，遊丹綺之重複。

translations.literal: Suddenly I was undeservedly appointed at Jianli and wandered the layered halls of cinnabar and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly I was undeservedly appointed at the Jianli Gate and wandered the layered halls of cinnabar and brocade.

sentences.zh: 信茲選之為難，乃上應於列宿。

translations.literal: Truly this selection was difficult—it even answered to the stars in the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: Truly this appointment was a hard choice—it even had to answer to the stars above.

sentences.zh: 陽源猶且自免，何稱仲治與太叔。

translations.literal: Yang Yuan still excused himself—how could one be called Zhongzhi or Taishu?
translations.idiomatic: Even Yang Yuan excused himself from office—how could one be called Zhongzhi or Taishu?

sentences.zh: 余生□之蕭散，本寓名而為仕。

translations.literal: My remaining life is □ and carefree; originally I only lodged my name and took office.
translations.idiomatic: My remaining life is □ and free of care; I had only lent my name to office in the first place.

sentences.zh: 好不存於吏法，才實疏於政理。

translations.literal: My tastes did not lie in clerkly law; my talent was truly thin in governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: My tastes had no place in clerkly law, and my talent was truly thin for governing affairs.

sentences.zh: 竟火燭之不事，徒博弈其賢已。

translations.literal: In the end I did not attend to urgent affairs by candlelight; I merely gambled at chess to prove my worth.
translations.idiomatic: In the end I did not burn the midnight oil at urgent business; I merely played chess to prove my worth.

sentences.zh: 竊自託於諸生，頗馳騁於文史。

translations.literal: Secretly I entrusted myself to the scholars and fairly ranged through literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly I cast my lot with the scholars and ranged freely through literature and history.

sentences.zh: 通人假其餘論，士林察於□理。

translations.literal: Men of insight borrowed my spare arguments; the forest of scholars judged me by □ principle.
translations.idiomatic: Men of insight borrowed my spare arguments; the forest of scholars judged me by □ principle.

sentences.zh: 乃妄涉於風流，遂飾輩於士子。

translations.literal: Then I rashly entered the world of elegant letters and at last adorned myself among gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Then I rashly entered the world of elegant letters and at last passed myself off among gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 且以自託，□□□□。

translations.literal: And so I entrusted myself □□□□.
translations.idiomatic: And so I entrusted myself □□□□.

sentences.zh: 雖邇傒塵滓，而賞許雲霞。

translations.literal: Though close to the dust and mire, I was praised as high as cloud and rosy light.
translations.idiomatic: Though I stood near the dust and mire, men praised me as high as cloud and rosy light.

sentences.zh: 栖閑虛以築館，背城闕而為家。

translations.literal: I dwelt in leisure and emptiness to build a hall and turned my back on the city gate to make a home.
translations.idiomatic: I dwelt in leisure and built a hall apart, turning my back on the city gate to make a home.

sentences.zh: 帶二學之高宇，遠三市之狹邪。

translations.literal: It bordered the high halls of the two academies and stood far from the narrow lanes of the three markets.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered the high halls of the two academies and stood far from the narrow lanes of the three markets.

sentences.zh: 事雖儉而未陋，製有度而不奢。

translations.literal: The affair was plain yet not crude; the design had measure and was not extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: The place was plain yet not crude; its design had measure and was never extravagant.

sentences.zh: 山隱勢於複石，水回流於激沙。

translations.literal: Mountains hid their slopes in layered stone; water turned back in eddies over rushing sand.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains hid their slopes in layered stone; water turned back in eddies over rushing sand.

sentences.zh: 樹先春而動色，草迎歲而發花。

translations.literal: Trees stirred with color before spring; grass met the year and sent forth flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Trees stirred with color before spring; grass met the new year and sent forth flowers.

sentences.zh: 座有清談之客，門交好事之車。

translations.literal: Within sat guests of pure discourse; at the gate came carriages of men who loved fine things.
translations.idiomatic: Within sat guests of pure discourse; at the gate came carriages of men who loved fine things.

sentences.zh: 或林嬉於月夜，或水宴於景斜。

translations.literal: Some frolicked in the groves by moonlight; some feasted on the water as the light slanted.
translations.idiomatic: Some frolicked in the groves by moonlight; some feasted on the water as the light slanted.

sentences.zh: 肆雕章之腴旨，咀文藝之英華。

translations.literal: They unfolded the rich flavor of carved prose and chewed the flower of literary art.
translations.idiomatic: They unfolded the rich flavor of carved prose and savored the flower of literary art.

sentences.zh: 羞綠芰與丹藕，薦朱李及甘瓜。

translations.literal: They set out green water-chestnuts and red lotus roots and offered red plums and sweet melons.
translations.idiomatic: They set out green water-chestnuts and red lotus roots and offered red plums and sweet melons.

sentences.zh: 雖慚洛水之名致，有類金谷之諠譁。

translations.literal: Though I was shamed before the fame of the Luo waters, it was still like the clamor of the Golden Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Though I fell short of the fame of the Luo waters, it still resembled the clamor of the Golden Valley.

sentences.zh: 聊自足於所好，豈留連於或號。

translations.literal: For a time it was enough for what I loved—how could I linger for some title?
translations.idiomatic: For a time it was enough for what I loved—how could I linger for some empty title?

sentences.zh: 思炯戒而自反，勗身名於所蹈。

translations.literal: I thought bright warning and turned back on myself, urging body and name along the path I trod.
translations.idiomatic: I took bright warning and turned back on myself, urging body and name along the path I trod.

sentences.zh: 奉哲后之淵猷，讚崇麾於華奧。

translations.literal: Serving the sage ruler's deep design, I praised the lofty banner in the splendid inner court.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the sage ruler's deep design, I praised the lofty banner in the splendid inner court.

sentences.zh: 豈千乘之乏使，感一眄之相勞。

translations.literal: Was it that a thousand chariots lacked envoys? I was moved by a single glance and personal labor.
translations.idiomatic: Was it that a thousand chariots lacked envoys? I was moved by a single glance and personal labor.

sentences.zh: 竟不留於三月，因病滿而休告。

translations.literal: In the end I did not remain three months; because my illness quota was full I asked leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the end I did not remain three months; when my sick leave was exhausted I asked to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 彼東觀之清華，乃任隆於載筆。

translations.literal: That Eastern Pavilion's pure splendor—there the charge was weighty for wielding the brush.
translations.idiomatic: That Eastern Pavilion's pure splendor—there the charge was weighty for wielding the brush.

sentences.zh: 蔡一去而貽恨，張再還而有述。

translations.literal: When Cai left once he left regret; when Zhang returned twice he had something to tell.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai left once he left regret behind; when Zhang returned twice he had something to tell.

sentences.zh: 忽牽短而濫官，司惇史於藏室。

translations.literal: Suddenly, though short in talent, I was wrongly given office and kept the solemn histories in the archive chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly, though short in talent, I was wrongly given office and kept the solemn histories in the archive chamber.

sentences.zh: 慚班子之繁麗，微馬生之簡實。

translations.literal: I was shamed before the Ban clan's ornate richness and fell short of Master Ma's plain truth.
translations.idiomatic: I was shamed before the Ban clan's ornate richness and fell short of Master Ma's plain truth.

sentences.zh: 復通籍而延寵，陪帝扃之華密。

translations.literal: Again I entered the rolls and received extended favor, attending the emperor's inner gate in splendid secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Again I entered the rolls and received extended favor, attending the emperor's inner gate in splendid secrecy.

sentences.zh: 信儀鳳之所栖，乃絲文之自出。

translations.literal: Truly where the ceremonial phoenix roosts—there silk writing issues of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Truly where the ceremonial phoenix roosts—there silk writing issues of itself.

sentences.zh: 歷五載而徘徊，猶官命之不改。

translations.literal: For five years I lingered, yet the official appointment did not change.
translations.idiomatic: For five years I lingered, yet the official appointment did not change.

sentences.zh: 謝能飛於無翼，故同滯於有待。

translations.literal: Xie could fly without wings; therefore I likewise stalled in waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Xie could fly without wings; therefore I likewise stalled in waiting.

sentences.zh: 晚加秩於戎章，乃□號之斯在。

translations.literal: Late I received rank in the military register—there □ title stood.
translations.idiomatic: Late I received rank in the military register—there □ title stood.

sentences.zh: 屬運道之將季，諒冠屨之無礙。

translations.literal: It fell when the age's way was nearing its end; I trusted that cap and shoes would not hinder me.
translations.idiomatic: It fell when the age's way was nearing its end; I trusted that cap and shoes would not hinder me.

sentences.zh: 奄昇御於鼎湖，忽流哀於四海。

translations.literal: Suddenly the emperor ascended at Ding Lake; suddenly grief flowed through the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the emperor ascended at Ding Lake; suddenly grief flowed through the four seas.

sentences.zh: 昔漢命之中微，皇統於是三絕。

translations.literal: Formerly in Han's mid-decline the imperial line thrice ended.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in Han's mid-decline the imperial line thrice ended.

sentences.zh: 暨孝昌之陵陂，亦繼□而禍結。

translations.literal: At the Xiao Chang tomb-slope disaster also followed □ and calamity knotted.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xiao Chang tomb-slope disaster also followed □ and calamity knotted.

sentences.zh: 將小雅之詩廢，復三綱之道滅。

translations.literal: The Odes of Lesser Ya were abandoned; again the way of the three bonds was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes of Lesser Ya were abandoned; again the way of the three bonds was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 思跼蹐於時昏，獨沉吟於運閉。

translations.literal: I brooded cramped in the age's darkness and alone sank in thought as fortune closed.
translations.idiomatic: I brooded cramped in the age's darkness and alone sank in thought as fortune closed.

sentences.zh: 遂退處於窮里，不外交於人世。

translations.literal: Then I withdrew to a poor hamlet and did not mingle with the human world outside.
translations.idiomatic: Then I withdrew to a poor hamlet and did not mingle with the human world outside.

sentences.zh: 及數反於中興，驅時雄而電逝。

translations.literal: When restoration returned several times, the heroes of the age drove like lightning and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: When restoration returned several times, the heroes of the age drove like lightning and vanished.

sentences.zh: 既籍取亂之權，方乘轉圓之勢。

translations.literal: They already borrowed the power to seize disorder and were just then riding the momentum of turning the circle.
translations.idiomatic: They already borrowed the power to seize disorder and were just then riding the momentum of a turning wheel.

sentences.zh: 俄隙開而守廢，遂冠冕之毀裂。

translations.literal: Soon the breach opened and defense was abandoned; then cap and robe were torn apart.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the breach opened and defense was abandoned; then cap and robe were torn apart.

sentences.zh: 彼膏原而塗野，嗟衞肝與嵇血。

translations.literal: There the plain was grease and the wilds were painted; alas for Wei Zhi's liver and Ji Kang's blood.
translations.idiomatic: There the plain was grease and the wilds were painted; alas for Wei Zhi's liver and Ji Kang's blood.

sentences.zh: 何古今之一揆，每治少而亂多。

translations.literal: Why is ancient and modern one measure—each time order is brief and disorder abundant?
translations.idiomatic: Why is ancient and modern one measure—each time order is brief and disorder abundant?

sentences.zh: 盧遁身於東掖，荀窘迹於南羅。

translations.literal: Lu hid his body in the eastern side-gate; Xun cramped his tracks in the southern net.
translations.idiomatic: Lu hid his body in the eastern side-gate; Xun cramped his tracks in the southern net.

sentences.zh: 時獲逃於□阜，仍竄宿於巖阿。

translations.literal: For a time I escaped to □ hill and still lurked and lodged in cliff caves.
translations.idiomatic: For a time I escaped to □ hill and still lurked and lodged in cliff caves.

sentences.zh: 首丘急於明發，東路長其如何。

translations.literal: Longing for home mound was urgent at dawn; the eastern road—how long would it be?
translations.idiomatic: Longing for the home mound was urgent at dawn; the eastern road—how long would it be?

sentences.zh: 遽登舟而鼓柂，乃沿洛而汎河。

translations.literal: Hastily I boarded a boat and beat the oar, then followed the Luo and floated the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hastily I boarded a boat and beat the oar, then followed the Luo and floated the river.

sentences.zh: 騖寸陰於不測，競征鳥於歸波。

translations.literal: I raced the inch of shadow into the unknowable and competed with homeward birds on the returning waves.
translations.idiomatic: I raced the inch of shadow into the unknowable and competed with homeward birds on the returning waves.

sentences.zh: 時在所而放命，連百萬於山東。

translations.literal: At the time they acted by whim wherever they were and linked a million men east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they acted by whim wherever they were and linked a million men east of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 何信都之巨猾，若封豕與大風。

translations.literal: What great villains of Xindu—like a penned boar and a great wind!
translations.idiomatic: What great villains of Xindu—like a penned boar and a great wind!

sentences.zh: 肆吞噬於觜距，咸邑燼而野空。

translations.literal: They devoured at beak and claw; cities burned to ash and the wilds were empty.
translations.idiomatic: They devoured at beak and claw; cities burned to ash and the wilds were empty.

sentences.zh: 徑黎陽之寇聚，迫崖壘之渢隆。

translations.literal: I passed the bandit muster at Liyang and pressed the cliff ramparts' roaring heights.
translations.idiomatic: I passed the bandit muster at Liyang and pressed the cliff ramparts' roaring heights.

sentences.zh: 躁通川而鼎沸，矢交射於舟中。

translations.literal: The open river seethed like a cauldron; arrows crossed and shot into the boat.
translations.idiomatic: The open river seethed like a cauldron; arrows crossed and shot into the boat.

sentences.zh: 備百罹於茲日，諒陳蔡之非窮。

translations.literal: That day I endured a hundred calamities; truly the straits of Chen and Cai were not destitution.
translations.idiomatic: That day I endured a hundred calamities; truly the straits of Chen and Cai were not destitution.

sentences.zh: 乘虎口而獲濟，陵陽侯而迅往，得投憩於濮陽，實陶衞之舊壤。

translations.literal: Riding the tiger's mouth I still crossed; passing the Lord of Yang I swiftly went on and found rest at Puyang—the old soil of Tao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the tiger's mouth I still crossed; passing the Lord of Yang I swiftly went on and found rest at Puyang—the old soil of Tao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 望鄉村而佇立，曾不遙之河廣。

translations.literal: Gazing at the village I stood and waited; the river's breadth was not far.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the village I stood and waited; the river's breadth was not far.

sentences.zh: 聞虜馬之夕嘶，見胡塵之晝上。

translations.literal: I heard the barbarian horses neigh at evening and saw barbarian dust rise by day.
translations.idiomatic: I heard the barbarian horses neigh at evening and saw barbarian dust rise by day.

sentences.zh: 王略恢而廟勝，車徒發而雷響。

translations.literal: The royal plan was vast and the temple had victory; chariots and foot set out with thunder's roar.
translations.idiomatic: The royal plan was vast and the temple had victory; chariots and foot set out with thunder's roar.

sentences.zh: 扇風師之猛氣，張天罼之層網。

translations.literal: They fanned the wind-lord's fierce breath and spread heaven's net in layered mesh.
translations.idiomatic: They fanned the wind-lord's fierce breath and spread heaven's net in layered mesh.

sentences.zh: 裁一鼓而冰銷，俄氛祲之廓蕩。

translations.literal: At one drumstroke ice melted; soon the baleful air was cleared and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: At one drumstroke ice melted; soon the baleful air was cleared and scattered.

sentences.zh: 昔蘧生之出奔，覩亡徵於亂政。

translations.literal: Formerly when Qu Sheng fled abroad he saw the sign of ruin in disorderly government.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Qu Sheng fled abroad he saw the sign of ruin in disorderly government.

sentences.zh: 及季子之來反，乃君立而位定。

translations.literal: When the younger son returned, then the lord was established and the throne was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When the younger son returned, then the lord was established and the throne was fixed.

sentences.zh: 伊吾人之蕞爾，本無傒於衰盛。

translations.literal: Alas for my slight person—I originally had no hope in decline or ascent.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for my slight person—I originally had no hope in decline or ascent.

sentences.zh: 忻草茅而偃伏，且優遊於辰慶。

translations.literal: I rejoiced to lie low in thatched huts and for a time wandered at ease in the imperial celebration.
translations.idiomatic: I rejoiced to lie low in thatched huts and for a time wandered at ease in the imperial celebration.

sentences.zh: 復推斥於宦流，延光華於璽命。

translations.literal: Again I was pushed back into the stream of office and received the imperial seal's splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Again I was pushed back into the stream of office and received the imperial seal's splendor.

sentences.zh: 甫聞內侍之忝，復奉優加之令。

translations.literal: Just as I heard of the inner attendant's undeserved post, again I received the edict of special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Just as I heard of the inner attendant's undeserved post, again I received the edict of special favor.

sentences.zh: 何金紫之陸離，鬱貂玉之相映。

translations.literal: What a glitter of gold and purple; sable and jade gleamed against each other.
translations.idiomatic: What a glitter of gold and purple; sable and jade gleamed against each other.

sentences.zh: 時權定之云初，尚民心之易擾。

translations.literal: When power was first settled, the people's hearts were still easily disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When power was first settled, the people's hearts were still easily disturbed.

sentences.zh: 何建武之明傑，茂雄姿於天表。

translations.literal: How brilliant was Jianwu, with heroic bearing above the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: How brilliant was Jianwu, with heroic bearing above the heavens.

sentences.zh: 忽靈命之有歸，藉親均而爭紹。

translations.literal: Suddenly the numinous mandate had a destination; relying on kin ties they competed for succession.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the numinous mandate had a destination; relying on kin ties they competed for succession.

sentences.zh: 師出楚而飈發，旆陵江而雲矯。

translations.literal: Armies left Chu like a gale; banners crossed the river like clouds bending.
translations.idiomatic: Armies left Chu like a gale; banners crossed the river like clouds bending.

sentences.zh: 闢閶闔之崢嶸，端冕旒於億兆。

translations.literal: They opened the towering Bright Gate and set the crown and tassels straight before the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the towering Bright Gate and set the crown and tassels straight before the hundred millions.

sentences.zh: 神駕逝以流越，翠華飈而繚繞。

translations.literal: The spirit carriage passed in flowing flight; the emerald canopy streamed and wound.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit carriage passed in flowing flight; the emerald canopy streamed and wound.

sentences.zh: 苟命舛而數違，雖功深而祚天。

translations.literal: If fate is crooked and numbers go against one, though merit is deep, the throne's span rests with heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If fate is crooked and fortune turns against you, though merit runs deep, heaven alone decides how long the throne may last.

sentences.zh: 時難忽然已及，網羅周其四張。

translations.literal: Hardship suddenly arrived; nets and snares closed on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Hardship suddenly arrived; nets and snares closed on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 非五三之親暱，罕狥節於漢陽。

translations.literal: Not kin like the Five Emperors and Three Kings—few died for principle at Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Not kin like the Five Emperors and Three Kings—few died for principle at Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 彼百僚之冠帶，咸北面於西王。

translations.literal: Those hundred officials in caps and sashes—all turned north to the Western King.
translations.idiomatic: Those hundred officials in caps and sashes—all turned north to the Western King.

sentences.zh: 矧恩疏而任遠，固身存而義亡。

translations.literal: How much more when favor was distant and trust far—surely body survived but principle perished.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when favor was distant and trust far—surely body survived but principle perished.

sentences.zh: 及宸居之反正，振天網於頹綱。

translations.literal: When the imperial seat returned to right rule, the heavenly net was shaken out from the collapsed cords.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial seat returned to right rule, the heavenly net was shaken out from the collapsed cords.

sentences.zh: 甄大義以明罰，虛半列於周行。

translations.literal: Great principle was sifted to make punishment clear; half the ranks in the court procession stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Great principle was sifted to make punishment clear; half the ranks in the court procession stood empty.

sentences.zh: 乃褫帶而來反，驅下澤於故鄉。

translations.literal: Then I stripped my belt and returned, driving the lower marsh-cart to my old home.
translations.idiomatic: Then I stripped my belt and returned, driving the lower marsh-cart to my old home.

sentences.zh: 探宿志以內求，撫身途而自計。

translations.literal: I sought my long-held purpose within and weighed my life's path for myself.
translations.idiomatic: I sought my long-held purpose within and weighed my life's path for myself.

sentences.zh: 不詭遇以邀合，豈釣名以干世。

translations.literal: I did not meet fortune by crooked means to win alliance; how could I fish for fame to meddle with the world?
translations.idiomatic: I did not meet fortune by crooked means to win alliance; how could I fish for fame to meddle with the world?

sentences.zh: 獨浩然而任己，同虛舟之不繫。

translations.literal: Alone I was vast and entrusted myself to my own way, like an empty boat with no mooring.
translations.idiomatic: Alone I was vast and entrusted myself to my own way, like an empty boat with no mooring.

sentences.zh: 既未識其所以來，亦豈知其所以逝。

translations.literal: Since I had not yet known whence I came, how could I know whither I would go?
translations.idiomatic: Since I had not yet known whence I came, how could I know whither I would go?

sentences.zh: 於是得喪同遣，忘懷自深。

translations.literal: Then gain and loss were sent off alike, and forgetting lodged deep within.
translations.idiomatic: Then gain and loss were sent off alike, and forgetting lodged deep within.

sentences.zh: 遇物栖息，觸地山林。

translations.literal: Where things were met I rested; wherever earth was touched there were hills and forests.
translations.idiomatic: Where things were met I rested; wherever earth was touched there were hills and forests.

sentences.zh: 雖因西浮之迹，何異東都之心。

translations.literal: Though my tracks drifted west like floating weed, what difference from the heart of one who hid in the Eastern Capital?
translations.idiomatic: Though my tracks drifted west like floating weed, what difference from the heart of one who hid in the Eastern Capital?

sentences.zh: 願自託於魚鳥，永得性於飛沉。

translations.literal: I wish to entrust myself to fish and birds, forever attaining my nature in soaring and sinking.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to cast my lot with fish and birds, forever at home in flight and in the depths.

sentences.zh: 庶保此以獲沒，不再罪於當今。

translations.literal: Hoping thereby to preserve this and reach a natural end, and no longer be guilty before the present age.
translations.idiomatic: May this preserve me to a peaceful end, and keep me from offending the age I live in.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，遭母憂，還鄉里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign, he suffered his mother's death and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign, Li Xie entered mourning for his mother and returned home.

sentences.zh: 徵為魏尹，將軍如故，以禫制未終，表辭。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Intendant of the Capital District, his general rank unchanged; because the mourning observance had not yet ended, he submitted a memorial declining.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Intendant of the Capital District, retaining his general's rank, but because his mourning period was not yet complete he memorialized to decline.

sentences.zh: 朝議亦以為優，仍許其讓。

translations.literal: Court deliberation also deemed it admirable, and still granted his request to decline.
translations.idiomatic: The court found his refusal admirable and allowed him to stand aside.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍求通和好，朝廷盛選行人，以諧兼散騎常侍，為聘使主。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sought friendly relations; the court carefully selected envoys, appointing Xie as concurrent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and chief of the diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan asked for peace and good relations, the court chose its envoys with care and appointed Li Xie concurrent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and head of the embassy.

sentences.zh: 諧至石頭，蕭衍遣其主客郎范胥當接。

translations.literal: When Xie reached Stone City, Xiao Yan sent his Master of Guests Fan Xu to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xie reached Stone City, where Xiao Yan sent his Master of Guests, Fan Xu, to receive him.

sentences.zh: 諧問胥曰：「主客在郎官幾時？

translations.literal: Xie asked Xu: "How long have you served as Master of Guests among the gentleman attendants?
translations.idiomatic: Li Xie asked Fan Xu, "How long have you held the post of Master of Guests among the gentleman attendants?

sentences.zh: 」胥答曰：「我本訓冑虎門，適復今任。

translations.literal: " Xu answered: "I was originally educated at the Tiger Gate Academy; I have only just resumed this present appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Xu answered, "I was trained at the Tiger Gate Academy and have only just taken up this present assignment.

sentences.zh: 」諧言：「國子博士不應左轉為郎。

translations.literal: " Xie said: "An Erudite of the National University ought not be demoted to a gentleman attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie said, "An Erudite of the National University ought not be demoted to a gentleman attendant.

sentences.zh: 」胥答曰：「特為應接遠賓，故權兼耳。

translations.literal: " Xu answered: "It is solely to receive distant guests; hence I am only temporarily assigned to the post.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Xu answered, "This is only to receive guests from afar, so I am temporarily holding the post.

sentences.zh: 」諧言：「屈己濟務，誠得事宜。

translations.literal: " Xie said: "Humbling oneself to serve the task—truly appropriate to the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie said, "To humble oneself for the sake of duty is indeed the right thing to do.

sentences.zh: 由我一介行人，令卿左轉。

translations.literal: Because of a mere envoy like me, you have been demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a mere envoy like me, you have been demoted.

sentences.zh: 」胥答曰：「自顧菲薄，不足對揚盛美，豈敢言屈。

translations.literal: " Xu answered: "Considering my own lack of merit, I am insufficient to respond to and proclaim such grandeur—how dare I speak of being humbled?
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Xu answered, "I am too slight in talent to answer and proclaim such grandeur—how dare I speak of being humbled?

sentences.zh: 」胥問曰：「今猶尚暖，北間當小寒於此？

translations.literal: " Xu asked: "It is still warm now; must the northern region be somewhat colder than here?
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Xu asked, "It is still warm now; must the north be a little colder than here?

sentences.zh: 」諧答曰：「地居陰陽之正，寒暑適時，不知多少。

translations.literal: " Xie answered: "The land lies in the correct balance of yin and yang; cold and heat come at their proper seasons—I do not know how much difference there is.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie answered, "The land stands in the true balance of yin and yang, and cold and heat arrive in season—I do not know how much difference there is.

sentences.zh: 」胥曰：「所訪鄴下，豈是測影之地？

translations.literal: " Xu said: "The Ye you speak of—is that truly a place for measuring shadows?
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Xu said, "The Ye of which you speak—is that truly a place for measuring the gnomon's shadow?

sentences.zh: 」諧答曰：「皆是皇居帝里，相去不遠，可得統而言之。

translations.literal: " Xie answered: "They are all imperial capitals and seats of emperors, not far apart—one may speak of them together as a whole.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie answered, "They are all seats of emperors and imperial capitals, not far apart; one may speak of them together.

sentences.zh: 」胥曰：「洛陽既稱盛美，何事遷鄴？

translations.literal: " Xu said: "If Luoyang was already called splendid and beautiful, why move the capital to Ye?
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Xu said, "If Luoyang was already praised as splendid, why move the capital to Ye?

sentences.zh: 」諧答曰：「不常厥邑，于茲五邦，王者無外，所在關河，復何所怪？

translations.literal: " Xie answered: "Not fixing one's seat permanently—with five capitals to this point—the ruler has no 'outside'; wherever lie the passes and rivers—what is there to wonder at?
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie answered, "Not dwelling forever in one place—with five capitals to this point—the ruler knows no 'outside'; wherever stand the passes and rivers, what is there to wonder at?

sentences.zh: 」胥曰：「殷人否危，故遷相耿，貴朝何為而遷？

translations.literal: " Xu said: "The Yin people were in peril and decline, so they moved to Xiang and Geng—why did your honored dynasty move?
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Xu said, "The Yin people were in peril and decline, so they moved to Xiang and Geng—why did your dynasty move its capital?

sentences.zh: 」諧答：「聖人藏往知來，相時而動，何必俟於隆替？

translations.literal: " Xie answered: "The sage stores up the past and knows what is to come; he acts according to the times—why must he wait for rise and fall?
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie answered, "The sage preserves the past and foreknows the future; he moves with the times—why must he wait for dynastic rise and fall?

sentences.zh: 」胥曰：「金陵王氣兆於先代，黃旗紫蓋，本出東南，君臨萬邦，故宜在此。

translations.literal: " Xu said: "The royal aura of Jinling was foretold in earlier generations; the yellow banner and purple canopy originate in the southeast—to rule all realms, the capital ought to be here.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Xu said, "The royal aura of Jinling was foretold in earlier ages; the yellow banner and purple canopy arise in the southeast—to rule the myriad realms, the capital ought to be here.

sentences.zh: 」諧答曰：「帝王符命，豈得與中國比隆？

translations.literal: " Xie answered: "The imperial mandate of a ruler—how can it be compared in grandeur with the Central States?
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie answered, "The mandate of a true emperor—how can it be compared in grandeur with the Central States?

sentences.zh: 紫蓋黃旗，終於入洛，無乃自害也？

translations.literal: The purple canopy and yellow banner will in the end enter Luoyang—is that not self-defeating?
translations.idiomatic: The purple canopy and yellow banner will in the end enter Luoyang—is that not cutting your own throat?

sentences.zh: 有口之說，乃是俳諧，亦何足道！

translations.literal: Mere spoken gossip is but wordplay—what is there worth mentioning!
translations.idiomatic: Mere talk on everyone's lips is only wordplay—what is there worth saying!

sentences.zh: 」蕭衍親問諧曰：「魏朝人士，德行四科之徒凡有幾人？

translations.literal: " Xiao Yan personally asked Xie: "Among the men of Wei, how many are there of the Four Categories of virtue and conduct?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao Yan himself asked Li Xie, "Among the men of Wei, how many belong to the Four Categories of virtue and conduct?

sentences.zh: 」諧對曰：「本朝多士，義等如林，文武賢才，布在列位，四科之美，非無其人，庸短造次，無以備啟。

translations.literal: " Xie replied: "Our dynasty has many scholars, righteousness equal to a forest; worthy talents in civil and military affairs fill every post. There are indeed men of the beauty of the Four Categories—but I am crude and ill-prepared, and cannot adequately report.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie replied, "Our dynasty has many scholars, righteousness thick as a forest; civil and military worthies fill every post. There are indeed men who embody the Four Categories—but I am too crude and unprepared to report them all.

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「武王有亂臣十人，魏雖人物之盛，豈得頓如卿言？

translations.literal: " Yan said: "King Wu had ten ministers who brought order—though Wei is abundant in men, can it truly stand comparison with what you say?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao Yan said, "King Wu had ten ministers who brought order—though Wei is rich in talent, can it really match what you describe?

sentences.zh: 」諧曰：「愚謂周稱十人，本舉佐命，至於『濟濟多士』，實是文王之詩。

translations.literal: " Xie said: "I think that when Zhou speaks of ten men, it refers only to those who assisted the mandate; as for 'The many scholars, in full array,' that is in fact a poem of King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie said, "I take it that when Zhou speaks of ten men, it means those who aided the mandate; as for 'The many scholars, in full array,' that is in fact a poem of King Wen.

sentences.zh: 皇朝廊廟之才，足與周人有競。

translations.literal: The talents of our dynasty who serve in court and temple are fully able to compete with the men of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The talents of our court are fully able to stand comparison with the men of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「若爾，文足標異、武有冠絕者，便可指陳。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "If so, those whose civil attainments stand out, or whose martial prowess is matchless—you may point them out and describe them.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao Yan said, "If so, name those whose civil attainments are outstanding or whose martial prowess is unmatched.

sentences.zh: 」諧曰：「大丞相勃海王秉文經武，左右皇極，畫一九州，懸衡四海。

translations.literal: " Xie said: "The Grand Chancellor, Prince of Bohai, combines civil and military mastery, supports the imperial throne, plans the governance of the Nine Provinces, and holds the balance over the Four Seas.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xie said, "The Grand Chancellor, Prince of Bohai, unites civil and military mastery, steadies the imperial throne, unifies governance across the Nine Provinces, and holds the scales over the Four Seas.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書、汝陽王元叔昭、尚書令元世儁，宗室之秀，綰政朝端。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Prince of Ruyang Yuan Shuzhao and Director Yuan Shijun—outstanding scions of the imperial clan who hold the reins of government at court.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Prince of Ruyang Yuan Shuzhao and Director Yuan Shijun—outstanding scions of the imperial house who hold the reins of government at court.

sentences.zh: 左僕射司馬子如、右僕射高隆之，並時譽民英，勠力匡輔。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Sima Ziru and Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi—both famed as the finest men of the age, striving together to support and assist.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Sima Ziru and Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi—both celebrated as the finest men of the age, laboring together to support the throne.

sentences.zh: 侍中高岳、侍中孫騰，勳賢忠亮，宣讚王猷。

translations.literal: Attendants-in-Chief Gao Yue and Sun Teng—meritorious, worthy, loyal, and upright, proclaiming and praising the kingly plan.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants-in-Chief Gao Yue and Sun Teng—meritorious, worthy, loyal, and upright, proclaiming and advancing the royal design.

sentences.zh: 自餘才美不可具悉。

translations.literal: As for the rest, their talents and excellences cannot all be recounted in detail.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest, their talents and virtues cannot all be recounted.

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「故宜輔弼幼主，永固基業，深不可言。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "So they ought to assist the young ruler and forever secure the foundation of the enterprise—profound beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao Yan said, "So they ought to assist the young ruler and secure the foundation forever—profound beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」江南稱其才辯。

translations.literal: The south of the Yangzi praised his talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: The lands south of the Yangzi praised his talent and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 使還，除大司農卿，加驃騎將軍，轉祕書監。

translations.literal: On return from the mission, he was appointed Minister of Grand Agriculture, promoted to General of Flying Cavalry, and transferred to Director of the Secretariat Library.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the embassy, he was appointed Minister of Grand Agriculture, promoted to General of Flying Cavalry, and made Director of the Secretariat Library.

sentences.zh: 遇偏風廢頓。

translations.literal: He suffered hemiplegia and was debilitated.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered a stroke that left half his body paralyzed.

sentences.zh: 武定二年卒，年四十九，時人悼惜之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding he died at age forty-nine; people of the time mourned and lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuding he died at forty-nine, to the grief of all who knew him.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、衞尉卿、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Grand General of Flying Cavalry, Minister of the Guard, and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand General of Flying Cavalry, Minister of the Guard, and Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 所著文集，別有集錄行於世。

translations.literal: The collected writings he authored circulated separately in a catalog of his collections.
translations.idiomatic: The collected works he authored circulated separately in a catalog of his writings.

sentences.zh: 長子嶽，武定末，司徒祭酒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yue, at the end of Wuding, was Libationer of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yue, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Libationer of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 嶽弟庶，尚書南主客郎。

translations.literal: Yue's younger brother Shu was Gentleman Master of Guests for the South at the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's younger brother Shu served as Gentleman Master of Guests for the South in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 諧弟邕，字修穆。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Yong, courtesy name Xiumu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xie's younger brother Yong, courtesy name Xiumu.

sentences.zh: 幼而儁爽，有逸才。

translations.literal: From childhood he was brilliant and open; he possessed exceptional talent.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was brilliant and free-spirited, with exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎、高陽王雍友。

translations.literal: Associate Gentleman of the Editorial Office; companion to Prince of Gaoyang, Yuan Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Associate Gentleman of the Editorial Office and as companion to Prince of Gaoyang, Yuan Yong.

sentences.zh: 凡所交遊皆倍年，儁秀才藻之美，為時所稱。

translations.literal: All his companions in friendship were twice his age; the beauty of his talent and literary refinement was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: All his friends were twice his age, yet the brilliance of his talent and prose won praise throughout the age.

sentences.zh: 年二十五，卒。

translations.literal: At age twenty-five he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮遠將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as General Who Subdues the Distance and Governor of Luozhou, with posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Subdues the Distance and Governor of Luozhou, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：邢巒以文武才策，當軍國之任，內參機揆，外寄折衝，其緯世之器歟？

translations.literal: The historian writes: Xing Luan, with his civil and military talent and strategy, shouldered the burdens of army and state—counseling in inner policy-making, entrusted with repelling enemies abroad—is he not an instrument to weave order across an age?
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Xing Luan, with civil and military talent and strategic counsel, bore the burdens of army and state—counseling within, repelling enemies without—is he not an instrument to order an age?

sentences.zh: 李平以高明幹略，効智於時，出入當官，功名克著，蓋贊務之英也。

translations.literal: Li Ping, with his lofty clarity and practical wisdom, applied his intelligence to the times; advancing and withdrawing in office, his merit and fame were fully achieved—he was surely a hero of supporting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping, with lofty clarity and practical wisdom, applied his intelligence to the times; in every office he held, merit and fame followed—surely a hero among those who sustain the state.

translations.idiomatic: "A man of Mo in Hejian commandery": in various editions "Mo" is erroneously written "Zheng"; the text is now emended according to the Beishi biography of Xing Luan (juan 43).

translations.idiomatic: "Champion General Lu Fangda fortified Nan'an": in various editions "Lu" is written "Zeng"; Zizhi Tongjian juan 146

translations.literal: "Lu Fangda" appears repeatedly in juan 8, Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong, second year of Zhengshi, and juan 98, biography of Xiao Yan; he was an important Liang general in this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: "Lu Fangda" appears repeatedly in juan 8 (Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong), second year of Zhengshi, and juan 98 (biography of Xiao Yan); he was an important Liang general in this campaign.

sentences.zh: 梁書卷一０鄧元起傳中也幾次提到他，當時別無「曾方達」其人。

translations.literal: The Liangshu juan 10 biography of Deng Yuanqi also mentions him several times; there was no person named "Zeng Fangda" at the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangshu biography of Deng Yuanqi (juan 10) also mentions him several times; there was no person named "Zeng Fangda" at the time.

sentences.zh: 「曾」乃「魯」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Zeng" is an error for "Lu"; the text is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Zeng" is an error for "Lu"; the text is now emended accordingly.

translations.literal: "Xiao Yuanzao was a silk-clad dandy of youth": in various editions "silk-clad dandy" (裙屐) is written "crowd play" (羣劇); Beishi juan 43 and Zizhi Tongjian juan 146
translations.idiomatic: "Xiao Yuanzao was a silk-clad dandy of youth": in various editions "silk-clad dandy" is written "crowd play"; Beishi juan 43 and Zizhi Tongjian juan 146

sentences.zh: 便戮鄧元起 諸本「起」作「超」。

translations.literal: "At once executed Deng Yuanqi": in various editions "Qi" (起) is written "Chao" (超).
translations.idiomatic: "At once executed Deng Yuanqi": in various editions "Qi" is written "Chao."

sentences.zh: 按蕭淵藻殺鄧元起，事見南史卷五五鄧元起傳。

translations.literal: According to records, Xiao Yuanzao killed Deng Yuanqi; the matter appears in Nanshi juan 55, biography of Deng Yuanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yuanzao's killing of Deng Yuanqi is recorded in the Nanshi biography of Deng Yuanqi (juan 55).

sentences.zh: 梁書卷一０鄧元起傳說元起「被收付州獄，於獄自縊」，微異，但死於淵藻之手的是鄧元起則一，「超」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: The Liangshu juan 10 biography of Deng Yuanqi says Yuanqi "was arrested and handed over to the provincial prison, where he hanged himself in custody"—a slight difference—but that he died at Yuanzao's hands is the same; "Chao" is erroneous and is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangshu biography of Deng Yuanqi (juan 10) says Yuanqi "was arrested and handed over to the provincial prison, where he hanged himself in custody"—a slight difference—but that he died at Yuanzao's hands is the same; "Chao" is erroneous and is now corrected.

translations.idiomatic: After "bi" there are the two characters "Dao Qian"; "yi" (議) is written "yi" (義).

sentences.zh: 按上二字當是通鑑所增，「議」疑當作「義」。

translations.literal: The two characters above were likely added by the Tongjian; "yi" (議) is suspected to read "yi" (義).
translations.idiomatic: The two characters above were likely added by the Tongjian; "yi" (議) is suspected to read "yi" (義).

translations.idiomatic: "General of Valiant Cavalry Xiang Wenyu and others led ten thousand troops to encamp at Gushan": Cefu juan 313

sentences.zh: 按卷八世宗紀正始三年七月丙寅稱「衍將桓和寇孤山，陷固城」，八月壬寅又稱「邢巒破蕭衍將桓和於孤山」。

translations.literal: According to juan 8, Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong, third year of Zhengshi, seventh month, day bingyin, it says "Yan's general Huan He raided Gushan and took Gucheng"; eighth month, day renyin, it again says "Xing Luan defeated Xiao Yan's general Huan He at Gushan."
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 8 (Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong), third year of Zhengshi, seventh month, day bingyin, it reads "Yan's general Huan He raided Gushan and took Gucheng"; eighth month, day renyin, it again reads "Xing Luan defeated Xiao Yan's general Huan He at Gushan."

sentences.zh: 卷九八蕭衍傳同，並不見所謂「相文玉」。

translations.literal: Juan 98, biography of Xiao Yan, agrees, and nowhere appears the supposed "Xiang Wenyu."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 98 (biography of Xiao Yan) agrees, and nowhere appears the supposed "Xiang Wenyu."

translations.literal: Also reads "Huan He encamped at Gushan"; yet this biography twice mentions "Wenyu" below, and the Tongjian both times reads "He."
translations.idiomatic: Also reads "Huan He encamped at Gushan"; yet this biography twice mentions "Wenyu" below, and the Tongjian both times reads "He."

sentences.zh: 則司馬光所見魏書當作「桓文玉」，故認為「文玉」即「桓和」。

translations.literal: Thus the Book of Wei as seen by Sima Guang should read "Huan Wenyu"; hence he identified "Wenyu" with "Huan He."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Wei as seen by Sima Guang should read "Huan Wenyu"; hence he identified "Wenyu" with "Huan He."

translations.idiomatic: Here "Xiang" is likely an error for "Huan"; "Wenyu" may be the character "He."
